title: حِكَايَةُ الْخَيَّاطِ
titleEn: The Tailor's Tale, continued: the Lame Young Man and the Barber
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 239–247 (Night 30, continuing directly from nights-29), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 30 continues the lame young man's story to the Tailor's company. The barber, who calls himself al-Ṣāmit ('the Silent') though he talks without end, recalls how the young man's father once paid him a hundred and three dinars for a poem, and keeps shaving, sharpening his razor and consulting his astrolabe while the young man frets about missing his tryst. He wrangles his way into the young man's feast, lists the grotesque friends he would rather dine with, and finally, left behind, tracks his master to the judge's house; there his shouting brings the young man's household and a crowd to the door, crying that their master has been killed. The night ends mid-scene as the judge asks what he has done. Verse is copied as printed. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلثَّلٰثِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānat al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-thalāthīna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fulfilling-one of the thirty.
sentences.i: And when the thirtieth night came,
sentences.n: The night-opening formula, here with a small gap in the print: the edition writes للثلثين without the alif of ثلاثين, so it is pointed with a dagger alif (ٰ) to read thalāthīn. الموفية is the feminine active participle of أَوْفَى, "to complete, fill out": the night that makes up the thirty.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الشَّابَّ قَالَ لَهُ إِنَّكَ قَاتِلِي فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-shābba qāla lahu innaka qātilī fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the-fortunate, that the young man said to him: "Indeed you are my killer on this day."
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the young man told him, "You will be the death of me today."
sentences.n: The formula that opens every night: Shahrazād picks up the tale where the last night left it. The speaker of qāla lahu is the young man (the lame one, narrating to the caliph), the addressee the barber, whose endless talk is about to kill him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنَا الَّذِي يُسَمُّونِي النَّاسُ الصَّامِتَ لِقِلَّةِ كَلَامِي دُونَ إِخْوَتِي السِّتَّةِ لِأَنَّ أَخِي الْكَبِيرَ اسْمُهُ الْبَقْبُوقُ وَالثَّانِي الْهَدَّارُ وَالثَّالِثُ فَنِيقٌ وَالرَّابِعُ اسْمُهُ الْكُوزُالْأَ سْوَانِيُّ وَالْخَامِسُ اسْمُهُ النَّشَّارُ وَالسَّادِسُ اسْمُهُ شَغَاشِقُ وَالسَّابِعُ اسْمُهُ الصَّامِتُ وَهُوَ أَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā sayyidī anā al-ladhī yusammūnī al-nāsu al-ṣāmita li-qillati kalāmī dūna ikhwatī al-sittati li-anna akhī al-kabīra ismuhu al-Baqbūqu wa-al-thānī al-Haddāru wa-al-thālithu Fanīqun wa-al-rābiʿu ismuhu al-Kūzu al-Aswānī wa-al-khāmisu ismuhu al-Nashshāru wa-al-sādisu ismuhu Shaghāshiqu wa-al-sābiʿu ismuhu al-Ṣāmitu wa-huwa anā
sentences.l: And he said: O my master, I am the one-who they-call-me, the people, the Silent, for the fewness of my speech, as-distinct-from my six brothers; because my brother the eldest, his-name (is) al-Baqbūq, and the second al-Haddār, and the third Fanīq, and the fourth, his-name (is) al-Kūz al-Aswānī, and the fifth, his-name (is) al-Nashshār, and the sixth, his-name (is) Shaghāshiq, and the seventh, his-name (is) al-Ṣāmit, and he is I.
sentences.i: The barber answered, "My lord, I am the man people call the Silent, because I say so little, unlike my six brothers. My eldest brother is named al-Baqbūq, the second is al-Haddār, the third Fanīq, the fourth is called al-Kūz al-Aswānī, the fifth al-Nashshār, the sixth Shaghāshiq, and the seventh is named al-Ṣāmit, and that is I."
sentences.n: The barber, his own ironic name "the Silent" set against a family of nicknames. Several mean something: baqbūq, "babbler, gurgler" (from baqbaqa, to babble); haddār, "a loud talker"; nashshār, "sawyer"; ṣāmit, "silent". Fanīq is a stallion camel in the lexicons, here evidently a nickname; Shaghāshiq is obscure to me. يُسَمُّونِي النَّاسُ is Middle Arabic: the verb takes the plural -ūna of "they" although the subject النَّاسُ follows it, and the relative الَّذِي is picked up by the pronoun -nī ("who they call me"). The print has الكوزالا سواني, which looks like الكوز الأسواني ("the Aswān jug") with the space misplaced after the alif of الأسواني; it is pointed here to keep both printed words as they stand.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا زَادَ عَلَيَّ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ بِالْكَلَامِ حَسِيتُ أَنَّ مَرَارَتِي انْفَطَرَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā zāda ʿalayya hādhā al-muzayyinu bi-al-kalāmi ḥasītu anna marāratī infaṭarat
sentences.l: And when this barber increased upon me with the talk, I felt that my gall-bladder had split.
sentences.i: But when this barber went on piling talk upon me, I felt that my gall bladder had burst.
sentences.n: The young man is speaking again. حَسِيتُ is Middle Arabic for classical حَسَسْتُ / أَحْسَسْتُ ("I felt"): the geminate verb has gone over to the weak pattern, as in colloquial. The gall bladder (مرارة) is the seat of courage and of temper; to have it burst is to be at the end of one's endurance. The print has no mark on عليّ here.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ لِلْغُلَامِ أَعْطِهِ رُبْعَ دِينَارٍ وَدَعْهُ يَنْصَرِفْ عَنِّي لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ فَلَا حَاجَةَ لِي بِحِلَاقَةِ رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-qultu li-al-ghulāmi aʿṭihi rubʿa dīnārin wa-daʿhu yanṣarif ʿannī li-wajhi Allāhi fa-lā ḥājata lī bi-ḥilāqati raʾsī
sentences.l: And I said to the lad: Give him a quarter of a dinar, and let him go-off from me for the face of God, for there is no need to-me of the shaving of my head.
sentences.i: And I said to my servant, "Give him a quarter-dinar and let him go away from me, for God's sake; I have no need of having my head shaved."
sentences.n: لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ, "for the face of God", is the stock plea of someone who wants to be rid of a burden or to have a thing done without reward. The jussive يَنْصَرِفْ after the imperative دَعْهُ ("let him go") is the regular construction.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ حِينَ سَمِعَ كَلَامِي لِلْغُلَامِ أَيْشْ هَذَا الْمَقَالُ يَا مَوْلَايَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla hādhā al-muzayyinu ḥīna samiʿa kalāmī li-al-ghulāmi ayshi hādhā al-maqālu yā mawlāya
sentences.l: And this barber said, when he heard my speech to the lad: What (is) this saying, O my master?
sentences.i: And when the barber heard what I said to my servant, he cried, "What kind of talk is this, my lord?"
sentences.n: أَيْشْ is the colloquial contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ, "what?", very common in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ لَآخُذُ مِنْكَ أُجْرَةً حَتَّى أَخْذُ مَكَ وَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ خِدْمَتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi lā ākhudhu minka ujratan ḥattā akhdhu maka wa-lā budda min khidmatika
sentences.l: By God, I will-not take from you a wage until I [serve] you, and there is no escape from serving you.
sentences.i: By God, I will take no fee from you until I have served you; serve you I must,
sentences.n: The print gives لآخذ, which can only be لا آخذ ("I will not take") with the two alifs run together: the sense demands a negative. In حتى اخذ مك the print seems to have split and garbled حتى أخدمك, "until I serve you" (ذ for د, and a stray space); the words are pointed as printed, and the translation follows the evident sense. The edition prints the vowel of لا آخذ as the madda of آ, which is kept.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُ وَاجِبٌ عَلَيَّ خِدْمَتُكَ وَقَضَاءُ حَاجَتِكَ وَلَا أُبَالِي إِذَا لَمْ آخُذْ مِنْكَ دَرَاهِمَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahu wājibun ʿalayya khidmatuka wa-qaḍāʾu ḥājatika wa-lā ubālī idhā lam ākhudh minka darāhima
sentences.l: For it (is) obligatory upon me, your service and the fulfilment of your need, and I do-not care if I do-not take from you dirhams.
sentences.i: For your service is my duty, and the meeting of your needs; and I do not mind if I take no money from you.
sentences.n: The subject (خِدْمَتُكَ وَقَضَاءُ حَاجَتِكَ) follows the predicate وَاجِبٌ, so the sentence is turned round for emphasis. The final دراهم is pointed as the diptote it is, without tanwīn.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ لَاتَعْرِفُ قَدْرِي أَنَا أَعْرِفُ قَدْرَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in kunta lā taʿrifu qadrī anā aʿrifu qadraka
sentences.l: And if you are not knowing my worth, I know your worth.
sentences.i: And if you do not know my worth, I know yours.
sentences.n: The print runs لا and تعرف together as لاتعرف; it is one printed word and is pointed as one. The pronoun أنا before the verb adds emphasis ("I, for my part").

sentences.t: وَكَانَ وَالِدُكَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَهُ عَلَيْنَا مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ كَرِيمًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna wāliduka raḥimahu Allāhu taʿālā lahu ʿalaynā mina al-iḥsāni li-annahu kāna karīman
sentences.l: And your father — God, may He be exalted, have-mercy on him — had upon us (some) of the benefaction, because he was generous.
sentences.i: Your father, God Most High have mercy on him, did us great kindnesses, for he was a generous man.
sentences.n: The prayer for the dead (رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ) is a parenthesis. The construction لَهُ عَلَيْنَا مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ is "he had upon us of kindness": the مِنْ is partitive, "a share of" or "much of".

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَرْسَلَ وَالِدُكَ خَلْفِي يَوْمًا بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ الْمُبَارَكِ قَدْ خَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi la-qad arsala wāliduka khalfī yawman bi-mithli hādhā al-yawmi al-mubāraki qad khaltu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: By God, indeed your father sent behind me one day, on the like of this blessed day; I had [entered] upon him.
sentences.i: By God, one day, a day just like this blessed one, your father sent after me, and I went in to him.
sentences.n: خَلْتُ is not a regular form: it is perhaps for دخلتُ (the first letter dropped), "I went in" — the natural sense with a company already present — or for خلوتُ, "I was alone with him", which does not fit the guests that follow; I read the first. أَرْسَلَ خَلْفِي is "sent behind me", i.e. sent after me, sent for me. بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ is "on a day like this", بـ marking the time.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عِنْدَهُ جَمَاعَةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَالَ لِى أَخْرِجْ لِي دَمًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿindahu jamāʿatun min aṣḥābihi fa-qāla lī akhrij lī daman
sentences.l: And there was with him a company of his companions, and he said to me: Bring-out for me blood.
sentences.i: He had a company of his friends with him, and he said to me, "Draw some blood for me."
sentences.n: أَخْرِجْ لِي دَمًا, "bring out blood for me", is the idiom for bloodletting, the barber's other trade (compare الحجامة below). The print writes لي with the final ى (لى) the first time and ي the second; both are kept.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ الِاصْطُرْلَابَ وَأَخَذْتُ لَهُ الِارْتِفَاعَ فَوَجَدْتُ الطَّالِعَ لَهُ نَحْسًا وَإِخْرَاجُ الدَّمِ فِيهِ صَعْبٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu al-iṣṭurlāba wa-akhadhtu lahu al-irtifāʿa fa-wajadtu al-ṭāliʿa lahu naḥsan wa-ikhrāju al-dami fīhi ṣaʿbun
sentences.l: So I took the astrolabe, and I took for him the altitude, and I found the ascendant for him ill-omened, and the drawing-out of blood in it difficult.
sentences.i: So I took my astrolabe and measured the altitude for him, and found his ascendant unlucky, and that letting blood at that time would be hard.
sentences.n: Medieval bloodletting was timed by the stars: the barber-physician took the sun's altitude with the astrolabe to cast the ascendant (الطالع) and see whether the hour was auspicious. وَإِخْرَاجُ الدَّمِ فِيهِ صَعْبٌ is a fresh clause (the print has the bare nominative-looking صعب, not the accusative that would continue the object): "and the drawing of blood in it is difficult".

sentences.t: فَأَعْلَمْتُهُ بِذَلِكَ فَامْتَثَلَ أَمْرِي وَصَبَرَ فَأَنْشَدْتُ فِي مَدْحِ—هِ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿlamtuhu bi-dhālika fa-imtathala amrī wa-ṣabara fa-anshadtu fī madḥi-hi
sentences.l: So I informed him of that, and he complied with my command and was patient, and I recited in praise of him.
sentences.i: I told him so; he heeded my advice and waited, and I recited these lines in his praise:
sentences.n: The print breaks مدحه with a dash (مدح—ه), apparently a line-end device; it is kept as printed and pointed on either side. أَعْلَمَ بِـ is "to inform of".

sentences.t:
اَتَيْتُ اِلَى الْمَوْلَى لِاِنْقَاصِ الدَّمِ * فَلَمْ اَرَوْقَتًا يَقْتَضِي صِحَّةَ الْجِسْمِ
جَلَسْتُ احَدِّثُهُ بِكُلِّ عَجِيبَةٍ * وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ اَنْشُرُ الْعِلْمَ مِنْ فَهْمِي
فَاَعْجَبَهُ مِنِّي السَّمَاعُ وَقَالَ لِي * تَجَاوَزْتَ حَدَّ الْفَهْمِ يَامَعْدِنَ الْعِلْمِ
فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَوْلَاكَ يَا سَيِّدَ الْوَرَى * اَفَضْتَ عَلَيَّ الْفَهْمَ مَا زَادَنِي فَهْمِي
كَاَنَّكَ رَبُّ الْفَضْلِ وَالْجُودِ وَالْعَطَا * وَكُنْزُ الْوَرَى فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْفَهْمِ وَالْحِلْمِ
sentences.tr:
ataytu ilā al-mawlā li-inqāṣi al-dami * fa-lam ara waqtan yaqtaḍī ṣiḥḥata al-jismi
jalastu uḥaddithuhu bi-kulli ʿajībatin * wa-bayna yadayhi anshuru al-ʿilma min fahmī
fa-aʿjabahu minnī al-samāʿu wa-qāla lī * tajāwazta ḥadda al-fahmi yā maʿdina al-ʿilmi
fa-qultu lahu lawlāka yā sayyida al-warā * afaḍta ʿalayya al-fahma mā zādanī fahmī
ka-annaka rabbu al-faḍli wa-al-jūdi wa-al-ʿaṭā * wa-kanzu al-warā fī al-ʿilmi wa-al-fahmi wa-al-ḥilmi
sentences.l:
I came to the master to reduce the blood * and saw no time that calls for the health of the body.
I sat telling him of every marvel * and before him I unrolled knowledge out of my understanding.
The listening to me delighted him, and he said to me * "You have passed the limit of understanding, O mine of knowledge."
And I said to him: "Were it not for you, O lord of mankind * you having poured understanding upon me, my understanding would not have increased me.
As if you were lord of bounty and generosity and giving * and the treasure of mankind in knowledge and understanding and forbearance."
sentences.i: I came to my lord to let his blood, but found no hour fit for the body's health. So I sat and told him every marvel, and spread out before him the learning of my mind. My hearing pleased him, and he said, "You have passed the bounds of understanding, O mine of knowledge." And I said, "Were it not for you, my lord, who poured knowledge upon me, my own wit would never have grown. You are the very lord of bounty, generosity and gift, and mankind's treasure in learning, wit and forbearance."
sentences.n: Five lines of verse in the rhyme -mi (الدم / الجسم / فهمي / العلم / الحلم). The edition points its verse, and every word here is copied as printed, including the unusual spacing of يَامَعْدِنَ (one printed word) and فَلَمْ اَرَوْقَتًا, which is فلم أر وقتا, "I saw no time", written together. In the last line الْعَطَا is spelt without its final hamza (العطاء), as often in verse. The printed alif carries no hamza throughout (اَتَيْتُ, اَعْجَبَهُ, اَفَضْتَ and so on); that is the edition's spelling, kept. The verse is the barber's flattery, a sample of the patter that gets him paid.

sentences.t: فَانْطَرَبَ وَالِدُكَ وَصَاحَ لِلْغُلَامِ وَقَالَ أَعْطِهِ مِائَةً وَثَلٰثَ دِينَارٍ وَخِلْعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-inṭaraba wāliduka wa-ṣāḥa li-al-ghulāmi wa-qāla aʿṭihi miʾatan wa-thalātha dīnārin wa-khilʿatan
sentences.l: And your father was moved-to-delight and called to the lad and said: Give him a hundred and three dinar, and a robe-of-honour —
sentences.i: Your father was delighted and called to his servant, saying, "Give him a hundred and three dinars, and a robe of honour,"
sentences.n: ثلث is the edition's defective spelling of ثلاث ("three"), pointed with the dagger alif; it cannot be "a third", as the next lines show (a hundred plus three single dinars). The singular دِينَارٍ after the numeral, instead of the plural, is Middle Arabic (the print has the plural دنانير a few lines later). انْطَرَبَ is the seventh-form of طَرِبَ, "to be moved to joy"; that form is post-classical.

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَانِي جَمِيعَ ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ أَتَتْ سَاعَةٌ حَمِيدَةٌ وَأَخْرَجْتُ لَهُ فِيهَا الدَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭānī jamīʿa dhālika ilā an atat sāʿatun ḥamīdatun wa-akhrajtu lahu fīhā al-dama
sentences.l: And he gave me all of that, until a praiseworthy hour came, and I drew out for him in it the blood.
sentences.i: And he gave me all of it. Then, when a propitious hour came, I drew his blood.
sentences.n: سَاعَةٌ حَمِيدَةٌ, "a praiseworthy hour", is an auspicious moment by the astrologers' reckoning.

sentences.t: وَلَا خَالَفَنِي وَشَكَرَنِى وَشَكَرُونِي الْجَمَاعَةُ الْحَاضِرُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-lā khālafanī wa-shakaranī wa-shakarūnī al-jamāʿatu al-ḥāḍirūna
sentences.l: And he did-not oppose me, and he thanked me, and they thanked me, the company, the present-ones.
sentences.i: He did not cross me in anything, and he thanked me, and the company who were there thanked me too.
sentences.n: Two Middle Arabic features: وَلَا with a perfect for "and he did not" (the classical negative of the perfect is مَا or لَمْ), and وَشَكَرُونِي الْجَمَاعَةُ with a plural verb ahead of its plural subject, الْجَمَاعَةُ الْحَاضِرُونَ, which also takes a masculine plural adjective. شكرنى is printed with the final ى; kept.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ خُرُوجِ الدَّمِ مَا أَمْكَنَنِي السُّكُوتُ حَتَّى قُلْتُ لَهُ بِاللَّهِ يَا مَوْلَايَ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda khurūji al-dami mā amkananī al-sukūtu ḥattā qultu lahu bi-Allāhi yā mawlāya
sentences.l: And after the going-out of the blood, silence was-not possible to-me until I said to him: By God, O my master —
sentences.i: But once the blood had flowed I could not keep silent, and I said to him, "By God, my lord,
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ is the oath-particle used as an entreaty: "I beg you by God".

sentences.t: مَا أَوْجَبَ قَوْلَكَ لِلْغُلَامِ أَعْطِهِ مِائَةً وَثَلٰثَ دَنَانِيرَ
sentences.tr: mā awjaba qawlaka li-al-ghulāmi aʿṭihi miʾatan wa-thalātha danānīra
sentences.l: What made-necessary your saying to the lad: Give him a hundred and three dinars?
sentences.i: what made you tell your servant, 'Give him a hundred and three dinars'?"
sentences.n: The syntax of مَا أَوْجَبَ قَوْلَكَ is not secure: I take it as "what made your saying (this) necessary?", i.e. "what was the reason for?"; another reading would make it an exclamation. ثلث is again the defective spelling of ثلاث.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ دِينَارٌ حَقُّ النِّجَامَةِ وَدِينَارٌ حَقُّ الْمُسَامَرَةِ وَدِينَارٌ حَقُّ الْحِجَامَةِ وَالْمِائَةُ دِينَارٍ وَالْخِلْعَةُ حَقُّ مَدْحِكَ لِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla dīnārun ḥaqqu al-nijāmati wa-dīnārun ḥaqqu al-musāmarati wa-dīnārun ḥaqqu al-ḥijāmati wa-al-miʾatu dīnārin wa-al-khilʿatu ḥaqqu madḥika lī
sentences.l: And he said: A dinar, the due of the star-reading, and a dinar, the due of the evening-conversation, and a dinar, the due of the cupping, and the hundred dinar and the robe, the due of your praise of me.
sentences.i: He answered, "One dinar is for the astrology, one for the pleasant talk, one for the bloodletting, and the hundred dinars and the robe are for your praise of me."
sentences.n: النِّجَامَةِ must mean astrology, reckoning by the stars (نجوم); I have not found the exact form in the lexicons, so its pointing is provisional. حِجَامَة is properly "cupping", and by extension bloodletting. وَالْمِائَةُ دِينَارٍ puts the definite article on the first term of a number phrase whose counted noun stays indefinite, which classical grammar does not allow; it is a Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَا رَحِمَ اللَّهُ أَبِي الَّذِي عَرَفَ مِثْلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā raḥima Allāhu abī al-ladhī ʿarafa mithlaka
sentences.l: So I said to him: May God not have mercy on my father, who knew the like of you.
sentences.i: And I said to him, "May God have no mercy on my own father, who knew a man like you!"
sentences.n: The sense of the outburst is not certain. Taken literally it is a curse on the speaker's father; as hyperbole it may mean that no one deserves mercy who knew so generous a man and did not profit by him, or it may be an ironic reversal of the formula رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ ("God have mercy on him") used earlier. Read it as the speaker's exclamation of astonished admiration, with the uncertainty noted.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ وَقَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُاللَّهِ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ يُغَيِّرُ وَلَا يَتَغَيَّرُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika hādhā al-muzayyinu wa-qāla lā ilāha illā Allāhu Muḥammadun rasūlu Allāhi subḥāna man yughayyiru wa-lā yataghayyaru
sentences.l: So he laughed, this barber, and said: "No god but God; Muhammad is God's-messenger! Glory to him who changes and is not himself changed."
sentences.i: At this the barber laughed and said, "There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God! Glory be to Him who changes all things and is Himself never changed."
sentences.n: رَسُولُاللَّهِ is printed as a single word. The closing phrase is the pious exclamation of wonder at how fortunes and people alter.

sentences.t: مَا كُنْتُ أَظُنُّكَ إِلَّا عَاقِلًا لَكِنَّكَ خَرِفْتَ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ
sentences.tr: mā kuntu aẓunnuka illā ʿāqilan lākinnaka kharifta mina al-maraḍi
sentences.l: I was not thinking-you except sensible; but you have grown-doting from the illness.
sentences.i: I always took you for a sensible man, but the sickness has made you dote.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْعَزِيزِ وَالْكَاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ وَالْعَافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla Allāhu fī kitābihi al-ʿazīzi wa-al-kāẓimīna al-ghayẓa wa-al-ʿāfīna ʿani al-nāsi
sentences.l: And God said in His mighty book: "and the restrainers of the rage and the pardoners from the people."
sentences.i: And God has said in His glorious Book: "... those who swallow their anger and pardon their fellow men."
sentences.n: A quotation from the Qurʾān (3:134), broken off after its first two clauses.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ مَعْذُورٌ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ وَمَا أَدْرِي سَبَبَ عَجَلَتِكَ وَأَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ أَبَاكَ وَجَدَّكَ مَاكَانَا يَفْعَلَانِ شَيْأً إِلَّا بِمَشُورَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-anta maʿdhūrun ʿalā kulli ḥālin wa-mā adrī sababa ʿajalatika wa-anta taʿlamu anna abāka wa-jaddaka mā kānā yafʿalāni shayʾan illā bi-mashūratī
sentences.l: And you (are) excused in every case, and I do not know the cause of your haste, when you know that your father and your grandfather were-not doing a thing except with my counsel.
sentences.i: You are excused in any case, but I cannot think why you are in such a hurry, when you know that your father and your grandfather never did anything without my counsel.
sentences.n: مَاكَانَا is printed as one word (mā kānā, "they were not"); with the imperfect it means "they never used to". شيأ is spelled as printed, with the hamza on an alif.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ إِنَّ الْمُسْتَشَارَ مُؤْتَمَنٌ وَمَاخَابَ مَنِ اسْتَشَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla inna al-mustashāra muʾtamanun wa-mā khāba mani istashāra
sentences.l: And it has-been-said that the consulted-one (is) entrusted, and he-has-not-failed who sought-counsel.
sentences.i: It is said that the man who is consulted is held in trust, and that no one who took counsel ever came to grief.
sentences.n: Two proverbs run together. وَمَاخَابَ is printed as one word (wa-mā khāba, "and he has not failed").

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَمْثَالِ مَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كَبِيرٌ فَلَيْسَ هُوَ بِكَبِيرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla fī baʿḍi al-amthāli man lam yakun lahu kabīrun fa-laysa huwa bi-kabīrin
sentences.l: And it has-been-said in some of the proverbs: he who has no elder, then he is not an elder.
sentences.i: And one of the proverbs says: whoever has no elder to guide him is himself no great man.
sentences.n: The bi- in بِكَبِيرٍ is the redundant bāʾ that often marks the predicate of laysa; it adds emphasis only.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And the poet has said:

sentences.t: اِذَا مَا عَزَمْتَ عَلَى حَاجَةٍ * فَشَاوِرْ خَبِيرًا وَلَا تَعْصِهِ
sentences.tr: idhā mā ʿazamta ʿalā ḥājatin * fa-shāwir khabīran wa-lā taʿṣihi
sentences.l: When you have resolved upon a need, * consult an expert, and do not disobey him.
sentences.i: When you are set upon some undertaking, take counsel of one who knows, and do not go against his advice.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels, kept exactly. After اِذَا the particle مَا adds nothing to the sense.

sentences.t: وَمَا تَجِدُ أَحَدًا أَعْرَفَ مِنِّي فِي الْأُمُورِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā tajidu aḥadan aʿrafa minnī fī al-umūri
sentences.l: And you will not find anyone more knowing than I in the affairs.
sentences.i: You will find no one who knows more than I do in such matters.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا وَاقِفٌ عَلَى أَقْدَامِي أَخْدِمُكَ وَمَا ضَجِرْتُ مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā wāqifun ʿalā aqdāmī akhdimuka wa-mā ḍajirtu minka
sentences.l: And I (am) standing upon my feet, serving you, and I have not grown-weary of you.
sentences.i: Here I stand on my own two feet, serving you, and I have never wearied of you.

sentences.t: فَكَيْفَ ضَجِرْتَ أَنْتَ مِنِّي وَأَنَا أَصْبِرُ عَلَيْكَ لِأَجْلِ مَالِأَبِيكَ عَلَيَّ مِنَ الْفَضْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-kayfa ḍajirta anta minnī wa-anā aṣbiru ʿalayka li-ajli mā li-abīka ʿalayya mina al-faḍli
sentences.l: So how have-you-grown-weary, you, of me, when I bear-patiently upon you for-the-sake of what (is) your father's upon me of the favour?
sentences.i: How is it, then, that you have wearied of me, when I bear with you for the sake of the kindness your father showed me?
sentences.n: مَالِأَبِيكَ is printed as one word: mā, "what", + li-abīka, "belonging to your father". The phrase says what the father holds over the speaker, namely the favour he did him.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ يَا ذَنَبَ الْحِمَارِ لَقَدْ أَطَلْتَ عَلَيَّ الْخِطَابَ وَزِدْتَ عَلَيَّ فِي الْمَقَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu wa-Allāhi yā dhanaba al-ḥimāri laqad aṭalta ʿalayya al-khiṭāba wa-zidta ʿalayya fī al-maqāli
sentences.l: So I said to him: "By God, O tail-of-the-donkey, you have indeed lengthened the address upon me and added upon me in the speech."
sentences.i: So I said to him, "By God, you donkey's tail, you have gone on at me far too long, piling word upon word."
sentences.n: "Donkey's tail" is an abusive vocative; the narrator, usually the polite one, loses his patience here.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا قَصْدِي أَنْ تَحْلِقَ رَأْسِي وَتَنْصَرِفَ عَنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-anā qaṣdī an taḥliqa raʾsī wa-tanṣarifa ʿannī
sentences.l: And I — my aim (is) that you shave my head and turn-away from me.
sentences.i: All I want is that you shave my head and leave me be.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَدْ بَلَّ رَأْسِي وَقٰلَ لِي قَدْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَكَ الضَّجَرُ مِنِّي لَكِنْ لَا أُؤَاخِذُكَ لِأَنَّ عَقْلَكَ ضَعِيفٌ وَأَنْتَ صَبِيٌّ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qad balla raʾsī wa-qāla lī qad ʿalimtu annahu dakhalaka al-ḍajaru minnī lākin lā uʾākhidhuka li-anna ʿaqlaka ḍaʿīfun wa-anta ṣabiyyun
sentences.l: Then he had wetted my head, and said to me: "I have known that the weariness entered you from me; but I do not take-you-to-task, because your mind (is) weak and you (are) a boy."
sentences.i: Then, having wetted my head, he said to me, "I know you have grown tired of me, but I hold nothing against you, for your wits are feeble and you are only a lad."
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال; it is pointed with a dagger alif (قٰلَ) so that it reads qāla and the spelling is untouched.

sentences.t: وَمَتَى كُنْتَ بِالْأَمْسِ كُنْتُ أَحْمِلُكَ عَلَى كَتِفِى وَأَمْضِي بِكَ إِلَى الْمَكْتَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-matā kunta bi-al-amsi kuntu aḥmiluka ʿalā katifī wa-amḍī bika ilā al-maktabi
sentences.l: And when you were — yesterday — I was carrying you upon my shoulder and going with you to the school.
sentences.i: Why, only yesterday, when you were small, I was carrying you on my shoulder and walking you to school.
sentences.n: The clause is elliptical: the sense is "when you were (little), only yesterday". كتفى is printed with final ى instead of ي and is kept so. المكتب is the elementary school where children learned the Qurʾān.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَاأَخِي بِحَقِّ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ اصْبِرْ عَلَيَّ حَتَّى أَقْضِىَ شُغْلِي وَقُمْ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā-akhī bi-ḥaqqi Allāhi ʿalayka iṣbir ʿalayya ḥattā aqḍiya shughlī wa-qum ilā ḥāli sabīlika
sentences.l: So I said to him: "O-my-brother, by the right of God upon you, be-patient upon me until I accomplish my business, and rise to the state of your way."
sentences.i: So I said to him, "Brother, I beg you in God's name, bear with me until I have finished my business, and then go your way."
sentences.n: يَاأَخِي is printed joined. أقضى ends in ى where Classical spelling has ي; kept as printed. قُمْ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ is a set phrase for "go on your way".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ شَقَقْتُ أَثْوَابِي
sentences.tr: thumma shaqaqtu athwābī
sentences.l: Then I tore my clothes.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآنِي فَعَلْتُ ذَلِكَ أَخَذَ الْمُوسَى وَسَنَّهُ وَلَا زَالَ يَسُنُّهُ حَتَّى كَادَ عَقْلِى يُفَارِقُنِى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾānī faʿaltu dhālika akhadha al-mūsā wa-sannahu wa-lā zāla yasunnuhu ḥattā kāda ʿaqlī yufāriqunī
sentences.l: And when he saw me do that, he took the razor and whetted it, and did-not cease whetting it, until my mind nearly left me.
sentences.i: When he saw me do that, he took up his razor and began to whet it, and he whetted and whetted until I thought my wits would leave me.
sentences.n: لَا زَالَ for the Classical مَا زَالَ is the Middle Arabic negative of "he kept on". عقلى and يفارقنى have final ى where one expects ي; kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى رَأْسِي وَحَلَقَ مِنْهَا بَعْضًا ثُمَّ رَفَعَ يَدَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma taqaddama ilā raʾsī wa-ḥalaqa minhā baʿḍan thumma rafaʿa yadahu
sentences.l: Then he advanced to my head and shaved some of it, then raised his hand.
sentences.i: Then he came up to my head and shaved off a part of it, and then lifted his hand.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا مَوْلَايَ الْعَجَلَةُ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَالتَّأَنِّي مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā mawlāya al-ʿajalatu mina al-shayṭāni wa-al-taʾannī mina al-raḥmāni
sentences.l: And he said: "O my master, haste (is) from the devil, and deliberation from the All-Merciful."
sentences.i: And he said, "My lord, haste comes from Satan, and deliberation from the Merciful."
sentences.n: A proverbial saying. التاني is printed without the hamza (al-taʾannī).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then he recited, saying:

sentences.t:
تَانَّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ لِامْرٍ تُرِيدُهُ * وَكُنْ رَاحِمًا لِلنَّاسِ تُبْلَى بِرَاحِمِ
وَمَا مِنْ يَدٍ اِلَّا يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَهَا * وَلَا ظَالِمٍ اِلَّا سَيُبْلَى بِظَالِمِ
sentences.tr:
taʾanna wa-lā taʿjal li-amrin turīduhu * wa-kun rāḥiman li-al-nāsi tublā bi-rāḥimi
wa-mā min yadin illā yadu Allāhi fawqahā * wa-lā ẓālimin illā sa-yublā bi-ẓālimi
sentences.l:
Be-deliberate and do not hasten for an affair you want, * and be merciful to the people; you will be tried with a merciful one.
And there is no hand but the hand of God (is) above it, * and no wrongdoer but he will be tried with a wrongdoer.
sentences.i: Take your time, and do not rush at a thing you long for; be merciful to people, and mercy will meet you. There is no hand but God's hand is over it, and every wrongdoer will in his turn be tried by a wrongdoer.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels, kept exactly. تَانَّ is printed without its hamza and is read taʾanna ("be deliberate"); لِامْرٍ likewise has a bare alif for li-amrin. In تُبْلَى بِرَاحِمِ the بِـ names what befalls you: you will be tried by one who is merciful (as you were).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا مَوْلَايَ مَا أَظُنُّكَ تَعْرِفُ بِمَنْزِلَتِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā mawlāya mā aẓunnuka taʿrifu bi-manzilatī
sentences.l: Then he said: "O my master, I do not think you know of my station."
sentences.i: Then he said, "My lord, I do not think you appreciate my standing."
sentences.n: عَرَفَ بِـ, "know of, be aware of", is a looser construction than the Classical direct object.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ يَدِي تَقَعُ عَلَى رُوُسِ الْمُلُوكِ وَالْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ وَالْحُكَمَاءِ وَالنُّضَلَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna yadī taqaʿu ʿalā ruʾūsi al-mulūki wa-al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi wa-al-ḥukamāʾi wa-al-nuḍalāʾi
sentences.l: For my hand falls upon the heads of the kings and the emirs and the viziers and the sages and the nuḍalāʾ.
sentences.i: For my hand falls upon the heads of kings, emirs, viziers, sages and the learned.
sentences.n: روس is printed without the hamza (ruʾūs, "heads"), as in the verse below. النضلاء looks like a misprint for الفضلاء, "the learned, the eminent" (nūn for fāʾ); it is pointed here as printed, on that assumption, and translated as the word that was probably meant.

sentences.t: وَ فِي قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa fī qāla al-shāʿiru shiʿrun
sentences.l: And in — the poet said — verse:
sentences.i: And the poet has said:
sentences.n: The stray وَ فِي before قَالَ makes no clear sense and is kept as printed; شعر, "verse", reads like a heading word introducing the lines.

sentences.t:
جَمِيعُ الصَّنَائِعِ مِثْلُ الْعُقُودِ * وَهَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ دَارُ السُّلُوكِ
فَيَعْلُو عَلَى كُلِّ ذِي حِكْمَةٍ * وَتَحْتَ يَدَيْهِ رُوُسُ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr:
jamīʿu al-ṣanāʾiʿi mithlu al-ʿuqūdi * wa-hādhā al-muzayyinu dāru al-sulūki
fa-yaʿlū ʿalā kulli dhī ḥikmatin * wa-taḥta yadayhi ruʾūsu al-mulūki
sentences.l:
All the crafts (are) like the necklaces, * and this barber (is) the house of the threads.
So he rises over every possessor of wisdom, * and beneath his two hands (are) the heads of the kings.
sentences.i: All the crafts are like strings of pearls, and this barber is the very house of their threads; so he towers over every man of wisdom, and under his hands lie the heads of kings.
sentences.n: The verse is printed with its vowels, kept exactly, including رُوُسُ for ruʾūsu without a written hamza. دَارُ السُّلُوكِ is pointed as "house of the threads" (the barber as the place where the strings of the crafts are gathered); the image is obscure and the reading uncertain. عُقُود can also mean "contracts".

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ دَعْ مَالَا يَعْنِيكَ فَقَدْ ضَيَّقْتَ صَدْرِي وَأَشْغَلْتَ خَاطِرِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu daʿ mā lā yaʿnīka fa-qad ḍayyaqta ṣadrī wa-ashghalta khāṭirī
sentences.l: And I said to him, "Leave what does not concern you, for you have narrowed my chest and occupied my mind."
sentences.i: And I said to him, "Leave what is none of your business, for you have worn out my patience and burdened my mind."
sentences.n: "Narrowing the chest" (ḍayyaqa ṣadra-) is the Arabic idiom for vexing someone past endurance; it returns a few lines below when the narrator’s own chest grows narrow. مَالَا is printed as one word: mā lā ‘what not’. أَشْغَلْتَ is the fourth-form verb ‘you have occupied’, a less common cousin of شَغَلَ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَظُنُّكَ مُسْتَعْجِلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aẓunnuka mustaʿjilan
sentences.l: And he said, "I think-you hasty."
sentences.i: Then he said, "I take it you are in a hurry."

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ نَعَمْ نَعَمْ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu naʿam naʿam naʿam
sentences.l: And I said to him, "Yes, yes, yes."
sentences.i: And I said to him, "Yes, yes, yes!"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ تَمَهَّلْ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ فَإِنَّ الْعَجَلَةَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَهِيَ تُورِثُ النَّدَامَةَ وَالْحِرْمَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla tamahhal ʿalā nafsika fa-inna al-ʿajlata mina al-shayṭāni wa-hiya tūrithu al-nadāmata wa-al-ḥirmāna
sentences.l: And he said, "Go-slowly upon your-self, for indeed the haste is from the devil, and it bequeaths the regret and the deprivation."
sentences.i: He said, "Take your time, for haste comes from Satan, and it leaves behind only remorse and loss."
sentences.n: عَلَى نَفْسِكَ ‘upon yourself’ is the ordinary way to say ‘easy does it’. تُورِثُ is ‘bequeaths, hands down as an inheritance’: haste leaves regret as its heirs.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَوةُ وَالسَّلَامُ خَيْرُ الْأَمْرِ مَاكَانَ فِيهِ تَأَنِّى
sentences.tr: wa-qad qāla ʿalayhi al-ṣalātu wa-al-salāmu khayru al-amri mā kāna fīhi taʾannin
sentences.l: And indeed he said — upon him the blessing and the peace — best of the affair is what there was in it deliberation.
sentences.i: And he has said — blessing and peace be upon him — "The best of undertakings is that in which there is deliberation."
sentences.n: The ‘he’ is the Prophet, and عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَوةُ وَالسَّلَامُ is the formula that follows his mention. تَأَنِّى is taʾannin ‘deliberation’, but the edition writes the final -in with ى; it is vocalised as printed. مَاكَانَ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا وَاللَّهِ رَابَنِي أَمْرُكَ فَأَشْتَهِي أَنْ تُعَرِّفَنِي مَا قَصَدْتَ عَلَيْهِ فَإِنِّي أَخْشَي أَنْ يَكُونَ شَيْأً غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā wa-Allāhi rābanī amruka fa-ashtahī an tuʿarrifanī mā qaṣadta ʿalayhi fa-innī akhshā an yakūna shayʾan ghayra dhālika
sentences.l: And I — by God — your affair has-made-me-uneasy; so I desire that you let-me-know what you have aimed at upon it, for I fear that it be something other than that.
sentences.i: And as for me, by God, your behaviour troubles me. I should like you to tell me what you have set your mind on, for I fear it is something else.
sentences.n: رَابَنِي (rāba) is ‘to cause someone misgiving’. Two spellings follow the Middle Arabic habit of writing final -ā as ي: فَأَشْتَهِي (‘I wish’, a verb Classical usage would not set before أَنْ like this) and أَخْشَي (Classical أَخْشَى). شَيْءًا is printed شيأ with the hamza as a bare seat; it is vocalised as shayʾan.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ بَقِيَ لِوَقْتِ الصَّلَوةِ ثَلٰثُ سَا عَاتٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qad baqiya li-waqti al-ṣalāti thalāthu sāʿātin
sentences.l: And there has remained until the time of the prayer three hours.
sentences.i: And there are still three hours left before the time of prayer.
sentences.n: ثلث is the defective spelling of ثَلَاث (hence the dagger alif), and the edition prints ساعات split in two, سا عات; it is read sāʿāt ‘hours’. لِوَقْتِ here marks the point the remaining time runs to: ‘left until the prayer-time’.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ مَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ بَلْ أُرِيدُ أَعْرِفُ الْوَقْتَ عَلَى التَّحْقِيقِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla mā urīdu an akūna fī shakkin min dhālika bal urīdu aʿrifu al-waqta ʿalā al-taḥqīqi
sentences.l: Then he said, "I do not want to be in doubt about that; rather I want I-know the time upon the verification."
sentences.i: Then he said, "I do not wish to be in doubt about it; I want to know the time exactly."
sentences.n: أُرِيدُ أَعْرِفُ sets one imperfect directly after another, without أَنْ (Classical أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ); this Middle Arabic juxtaposition is kept as printed and vocalised with the indicative.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ الْكَلَامَ إِذَا كَانَ رَجْمًا بِالْغَيْبِ كَانَ فِيهِ عَيْبٌ لَاسِيَّمَا لِمِثْلِي وَقَدْ ظَهَرَ وَاشْتَهَرَ عِنْدَ النَّاسِ فَضْلِي فَمَايَنْبَغِي لِي أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ حَدْسًا كَمَا تَتَكَلَّمُ عَامَّةُ الْمُنَجِّمِينَ
sentences.tr: li-anna al-kalāma idhā kāna rajman bi-al-ghaybi kāna fīhi ʿaybun lā siyyamā li-mithlī wa-qad ẓahara wa-ishtahara ʿinda al-nāsi faḍlī fa-mā yanbaghī lī an atakallama ḥadsan ka-mā tatakallamu ʿāmmatu al-munajjimīna
sentences.l: Because speech, when it is a stoning at the unseen, there is in it a fault — especially for one like me — and my excellence has become manifest and famed among the people; so it is not fitting for me that I speak by guess, as the common-folk of the astrologers speak.
sentences.i: For talk that is mere guessing at the unseen carries a fault in it, most of all in one like me, whose excellence is known and famed among the people; it is not fitting that I should speak by conjecture as the common run of astrologers do.
sentences.n: رَجْمٌ بِالْغَيْبِ (‘stoning at the unseen’) is the standing phrase for guesswork about what cannot be known. The edition prints فَمَايَنْبَغِي and لَاسِيَّمَا each as a single word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَمَى الْمُوسَى مِنْ يَدِهِ وَأَخَذَ الْاصْطُرْلَابَ وَمَضَى تَحْتَ الشَّمْسِ وَوَقَفَ مُدَّةً مَدِيدَةً وَعَادَ
sentences.tr: thumma ramā al-mūsā min yadihi wa-akhadha al-iṣṭurlāba wa-maḍā taḥta al-shamsi wa-waqafa muddatan madīdatan wa-ʿāda
sentences.l: Then he threw the razor from his hand, and took the astrolabe, and went off beneath the sun, and stood a stretched-out while, and returned.
sentences.i: Then he flung the razor from his hand, took up his astrolabe, and went out under the sun; there he stood a long while, and came back.
sentences.n: الْاصْطُرْلَابُ is the astrolabe, the instrument by which the sun’s height gives the hour; the barber poses as an astrologer.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ قَدْ بَقِيَ لِوَقْتِ الصَّلَوةِ ثَلٰثُ سَا عَاتٍ لَاتَزِيدُ وَلَاتَنْقُصُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla qad baqiya li-waqti al-ṣalāti thalāthu sāʿātin lā tazīdu wa-lā tanquṣu
sentences.l: And he said, "There has remained until the time of the prayer three hours; it does not increase and does not decrease."
sentences.i: And he said, "There are three hours left before the time of prayer, no more and no less."
sentences.n: لَاتَزِيدُ and وَلَاتَنْقُصُ are each printed as one word. The ‘it’ is the plural ‘hours’, with the feminine singular verb that Arabic uses for non-human plurals.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ اسْكُتْ عَنِّي فَقَدْ فَتَّتَّ كَبِدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka uskut ʿannī fa-qad fattatta kabidī
sentences.l: And I said to him, "By God upon you, be silent from me, for you have crumbled my liver."
sentences.i: And I said to him, "For God’s sake, I beg you, hold your tongue and let me be — you are tearing me to pieces."
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ is an oath-plea, ‘by God, I charge you’. The liver is the seat of feeling, so ‘crumbling the liver’ is breaking a person’s heart. The edition prints فتت for fattatta; the stem’s final t and the subject’s -ta are written as one letter, so it is vocalised with the shadda.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْمُوسَى وَسَنَّهُ كَمَا فَعَلَ أَوَّلًا وَحَلَقَ بَعْضَ رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-mūsā wa-sannahu ka-mā faʿala awwalan wa-ḥalaqa baʿḍa raʾsī
sentences.l: And he took the razor and whetted it as he did at first, and shaved some of my head.
sentences.i: So he took up the razor and whetted it, just as he had done before, and shaved a part of my head.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ أَنَا مَهْمُومٌ مِنْ عَجَلَتِكَ فَلَوْأَطْلَعْتَنِي عَلَى سَبَبِهَا لَكَانَ خَيْرًالَكَ لِأَنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ أَبَاكَ وَجَدَّكَ مَاكَانَا يَفْعَلَانِ شَيْئًا إِلَّا بِمَشُورَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla anā mahmūmun min ʿajlatika fa-law aṭlaʿtanī ʿalā sababihā la-kāna khayran laka li-annaka taʿlamu anna abāka wa-jaddaka mā kānā yafʿalāni shayʾan illā bi-mashūratī
sentences.l: And he said, "I am worried from your haste; so if you had informed me of its cause, it would have been better for you, because you know that your father and your grandfather used not to do anything except with my counsel."
sentences.i: Then he said, "Your haste worries me. Had you told me the reason for it, it would have been better for you, for you know that your father and your grandfather never did a thing without my counsel."
sentences.n: فَلَوْأَطْلَعْتَنِي (law + the fourth-form aṭlaʿa ‘to let someone know’) and خَيْرًالَكَ are each printed as one word; the lām of لَكَانَ opens the ‘then’ half of the if-clause. إِلَّا بِمَشُورَتِي, ‘except with my counsel’, is the barber’s boast that no house of note acted without him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ مَالِي مِنْهُ خَلَاصٌ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿalimtu anna mā lī minhu khalāṣun wa-qultu fī nafsī
sentences.l: And when I knew that there was not for me from him any deliverance, I said in my self,
sentences.i: When I saw that there was no escaping him, I said to myself,
sentences.n: The wa- on وَقُلْتُ opens the main clause after فَلَمَّا, a Middle Arabic habit (Classical Arabic would have no conjunction); it is kept as printed. مَالِي مِنْهُ خَلَاصٌ is ‘there is no deliverance for me from him’.

sentences.t: جَاءَ وَقْتُ الصَّلَوةِ وَأُرِيدُأَنْ أَمْضِيَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ النَّاسُ مِنَ الصَّلَوةِ
sentences.tr: jāʾa waqtu al-ṣalāti wa-urīdu an amḍiya qabla an takhruja al-nāsu mina al-ṣalāti
sentences.l: "The time of the prayer has come, and I want to go before the people (she) come out from the prayer;
sentences.i: "The hour of prayer has come, and I want to be off before the people come out from the service;
sentences.n: اريدان is printed as one word (urīdu an). النَّاسُ takes a feminine verb here (تَخْرُجَ), as a collective noun may; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ تَأَخَّرْتُ سَاعَةً لَأَدْرِي أَيْنَ السَّبِيلُ إِلَى الدُّخُولِ إِلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-in taʾakhkhartu sāʿatan lā adrī ayna al-sabīlu ilā al-dukhūli ilayhā
sentences.l: for if I am late an hour, I do not know where is the way to the entering to it."
sentences.i: for if I am an hour late, I shall not know how to get in."
sentences.n: لَأَدْرِي is printed لادري, one alif doing duty for both the alif of لَا and the hamza of أَدْرِي (lā adrī); it is not a lām of emphasis. إِلَى الدُّخُولِ إِلَيْهَا is ‘the way to entering it’, the second إِلَى belonging to the verbal noun.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ أَوْجِزْوَدَعْ عَنْكَ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَالْفُضُولَ فَإِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ أَمْضِيَ إِلَى دَعْوَةٍ عِنْدَ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu awjiz wa-daʿ ʿanka hādhā al-kalāma wa-al-fuḍūla fa-innī urīdu an amḍiya ilā daʿwatin ʿinda baʿḍi aṣḥābī
sentences.l: And I said, "Be brief and leave from yourself this talk and the meddling, for I want to go to an invitation at some of my companions."
sentences.i: And I said, "Be brief, and spare me this talk and idle meddling, for I am bound for a banquet at the house of a friend of mine."
sentences.n: أَوْجِزْوَدَعْ is printed as one word (awjiz wa-daʿ). الْفُضُولُ is officious busybodying, the chatter that is ‘beyond’ one’s business.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذِكْرَ الدَّعْوَةِ قَالَ يَوْمُكَ يَوْمٌ مُبَارَكٌ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa dhikra al-daʿwati qāla yawmuka yawmun mubārakun ʿalayya
sentences.l: And when he heard the mention of the invitation, he said, "Your day is a day blessed upon me."
sentences.i: When he heard the banquet mentioned, he said, "Yours is a blessed day, and blessed for me."

sentences.t: لَقَدْ كُنْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ حَلَفْتُ عَلَى جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ أَصْلِ قَائِي وَنَسِيتُ أَنْ أَهْتَمَّ لَهُمْ فِي شِي يَأكُلُونَهُ وَالسَّاعَةَ افْتَكَرْتُ وَافَضِيحَتَاهْ مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: la-qad kuntu al-bāriḥata ḥalaftu ʿalā jamāʿatin min aṣli qāʾī wa-nasītu an ahtamma lahum fī shī yaʾkulūnahu wa-al-sāʿata iftakartu wā-faḍīḥatāh minhum
sentences.l: "Indeed I had, last night, sworn upon a company from [aṣdiqāʾī] "my friends", and I forgot to take care for them in something they might eat; and just now I remembered — oh, the disgrace! — before them."
sentences.i: "Last night, you see, I had pressed a company of my friends with an oath to come, and I forgot to provide them with anything to eat. Only this moment have I remembered — oh, the shame of it before them!"
sentences.n: اصل قائي is printed as two words and gives no sense as it stands; it is most likely a misprint for أَصْدِقَائِي ‘my friends’ (ل for د), and is kept and vocalised as printed. حَلَفَ عَلَى is ‘to adjure, to bind with an oath’ (here, to come as guests). شِي is the short form of شَيْء, written without the hamza, as in speech. وَافَضِيحَتَاهْ is the cry of lament wā … -āh: ‘oh, the scandal of it!’

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ لَاتَهْتَمَّ بِهَذَا الْأَمْرِ بَعْدَ تَعْرِيفِكَ أَنَّنِي الْيَوْمَ فِي دَعْوَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu lā tahtamma bi-hādhā al-amri baʿda taʿrīfika annanī al-yawma fī daʿwatin
sentences.l: And I said to him, "Do not trouble yourself over this matter, after informing you that I am today at an invitation."
sentences.i: And I said to him, "Do not trouble yourself over this, now that you know I am at a banquet today."
sentences.n: بَعْدَ تَعْرِيفِكَ is ‘after (my) letting you know’: the -ka is the object of the verbal noun, and the speaker is understood.

sentences.t: فَكُلُّ مَا فِي دَارِي مِنْ طَعَامٍ وَشَرَابٍ فَهُوَلَكَ إِنْ أَنْجَزْتَ أَمْرِي وَعَجَّلْتَ حِلَاقَةَ رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-kullu mā fī dārī min ṭaʿāmin wa-sharābin fa-huwa laka in anjazta amrī wa-ʿajjalta ḥilāqata raʾsī
sentences.l: For everything that is in my house of food and drink, it is yours, if you complete my affair and hasten the shaving of my head.
sentences.i: Everything in my house in the way of food and drink is yours, if you finish my business and hurry the shaving of my head.
sentences.n: فَهُوَلَكَ is printed as one word (fa-huwa laka); the fa- opens the main clause. The speaker, in a corner, offers his whole table to be rid of the man.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا صِفْ لِي مَا عِنْدَكَ لِأَضْيَافِي حَتَّى أَعْرِفَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla jazāka Allāhu khayran ṣif lī mā ʿindaka li-aḍyāfī ḥattā aʿrifahu
sentences.l: And he said, "May God requite you good. Describe to me what is with you for my guests, until I know it."
sentences.i: He said, "God reward you well. Tell me what you have for my guests, so that I may know it."

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ عِنْدِي خَمْسَةُ أَلْوَانِ طَعَامٍ وَعَشْرُ دَجَاجَاتٍ مُحَمَّرَاتٍ وَخَرُوفٌ مَشْوِيٌّ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu ʿindī khamsatu alwāni ṭaʿāmin wa-ʿashru dajājātin muḥammarātin wa-kharūfun mashwiyyun
sentences.l: And I said, "With me are five colours of food, and ten hens browned, and a roasted lamb."
sentences.i: And I said, "I have five kinds of dishes, ten fried chickens, and a roast lamb."
sentences.n: أَلْوَانُ طَعَامٍ (‘colours of food’) means kinds of dish. مُحَمَّرَات are chickens browned in fat; خَرُوف is a lamb.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَحْضِرْهُمْ لِي حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ فَأَحْضَرْتُ لَهُ ذَلِكَ جَمِيعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aḥḍirhum lī ḥattā anẓura fa-aḥḍartu lahu dhālika jamīʿahu
sentences.l: And he said, "Bring them to me until I look"; and I brought him all of that.
sentences.i: He said, "Bring them to me, that I may see," and I brought him all of it.
sentences.n: أَحْضِرْهُمْ is ‘them’ in the masculine plural, though the dishes it points back to are things, not persons; kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَايَنَهُ قَالَ بَقِيَ الشَّرَابُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿāyanahu qāla baqiya al-sharābu
sentences.l: And when he inspected it, he said, "The drink remains."
sentences.i: When he had looked it over, he said, "There remains the drink."

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ عِنْدِي فَقَالَ أَحْضِرْهُ فَأَحْضَرْتُهُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu ʿindī fa-qāla aḥḍirhu fa-aḥḍartuhu lahu
sentences.l: And I said to him, "With me." And he said, "Bring it." And I brought it to him.
sentences.i: I told him I had some. He said, "Bring it," and I brought it to him.

sentences.t: قَالَ لِلَّهِ دَرُّكَ مَا أَكْرَمَ نَفْسَكَ لَكِنْ بَقِيَ الْبَخُورُ وَالطِّيبُ
sentences.tr: qāla li-Allāhi darruka mā akrama nafsaka lākin baqiya al-bakhūru wa-al-ṭību
sentences.l: He said, "To God your milk! How generous your soul! But there remain the incense and the perfume."
sentences.i: He said, "Bless you — how generous you are! But there remain the incense and the perfumes."
sentences.n: لِلَّهِ دَرُّكَ (‘to God be your milk’) is a stock cry of admiration: God be thanked for such a nature as yours. The sentence follows the previous one with no conjunction, as the narrative often does.

sentences.t: فَأَحْضَرْتُ لَهُ دُرْجَانِيَّةَ نَدٍّ وَعُودٍ وَعَنْبَرٍ وَمِسْكٍ يُسَاوِي خَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا
sentences.tr: fa-aḥḍartu lahu durjāniyyata naddin wa-ʿūdin wa-ʿanbarin wa-miskin yusāwī khamsīna dīnāran
sentences.l: And I brought him a durjāniyya of nadd and aloes-wood and ambergris and musk, equalling fifty dinars.
sentences.i: I brought him a casket of nadd, aloes-wood, ambergris and musk, worth fifty dinars.
sentences.n: درجانية is most likely a little chest with drawers (cf. دُرْج ‘casket, drawer’, which the text uses just below), but the word and its vowels are not certain. نَدّ is a compounded perfume, and عُود is aloes-wood, burnt as incense.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَقْتُ قَدْ ضَاقَ وَضَاقَ صَدْرِي
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-waqtu qad ḍāqa wa-ḍāqa ṣadrī
sentences.l: And the time had grown narrow, and my chest grew narrow.
sentences.i: By now the time was growing short, and my patience was wearing thin.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ خُذْ هَذَا وَاحْلِقْ لِي جَمِيعَ رَأْسِي بِحَيَاةِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu khudh hādhā wa-iḥliq lī jamīʿa raʾsī bi-ḥayāti Muḥammadin ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallama
sentences.l: And I said to him, "Take this, and shave for me the whole of my head, by the life of Muhammad — God bless him and give him peace."
sentences.i: And I said to him, "Take this, and shave my whole head, by the life of Muhammad, God’s blessing and peace upon him."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمُزَيِّنُ وَاللَّهِ مَا آخُذُهُ حَتَّى أَرَى جَمِيعَ مَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-muzayyinu wa-Allāhi mā ākhudhuhu ḥattā arā jamīʿa mā fīhi
sentences.l: And the barber said, "By God, I will not take it until I see the whole of what is in it."
sentences.i: The barber said, "By God, I will not take it until I have seen everything in it."

sentences.t: فَأَمَرْتُ الْغُلَامَ فَفَتَحَ لَهُ الدَّرْجَ فَرَمَى الْمُزَيِّنُ الْاصْطُرْلَابَ مِنْ يَدِةِ
sentences.tr: fa-amartu al-ghulāma fa-fataḥa lahu al-durja fa-ramā al-muzayyinu al-iṣṭurlāba min yadihi
sentences.l: And I ordered the lad, and he opened for him the casket; and the barber threw the astrolabe from his hand.
sentences.i: I ordered my servant, who opened the casket for him; and the barber let the astrolabe fall from his hand.
sentences.n: يَدِةِ is printed with ة where ه is meant (yadihi); the letter is kept and vocalised so that it reads yadihi. الدَّرْجُ, ‘the drawer’, is the casket just called دُرْجَانِيَّة.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ يُقَلِّبُ الطِّيبَ وَالْبَخُورَ وَالْعُودَ الَّذِي فِي الدَّرْجِ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasa ʿalā al-arḍi yuqallibu al-ṭība wa-al-bakhūra wa-al-ʿūda alladhī fī al-durji
sentences.l: And he sat on the ground, turning over the perfume and the incense and the aloes-wood that was in the casket,
sentences.i: and sat down on the floor, turning over the perfumes, the incense and the aloes-wood that lay in the casket,

sentences.t: حَتَّى ضَاقَ صَدْرِي ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَ وَأَخَذَ الْمُوسَى وَحَلَقَ مِنْ رَأْسِي شَيْئًا يَسِيرًا
sentences.tr: ḥattā ḍāqa ṣadrī thumma taqaddama wa-akhadha al-mūsā wa-ḥalaqa min raʾsī shayʾan yasīran
sentences.l: until my chest grew narrow; then he came forward and took the razor and shaved from my head a thing, slight.
sentences.i: until my patience was gone; then he came forward, took up the razor, and shaved a very little from my head.

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُ—ولُ
sentences.tr: wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And he recited, saying
sentences.n: The dash inside يق—ول is in the printed text (a break or a damaged letter-space); it is kept. The verses he recites lie beyond this stretch.

sentences.t: يَنْشُو الصَّغِيرُ عَلَى مَا كَانَ وَالِدُهُ * اِنَّ الْاُصُولَ عَلَيْهَا يَنْبُتُ الشَّجَرُ
sentences.tr: yanshū al-ṣaghīru ʿalā mā kāna wāliduhu * inna al-uṣūla ʿalayhā yanbutu al-shajaru
sentences.l: The small-one grows up upon what his father was * indeed the roots — upon them the tree grows.
sentences.i: The child grows up as his father was before him; the tree grows only upon its roots.
sentences.n: A proverbial verse. The edition prints it pointed, and the pointing is copied as printed, including اِنَّ and الْاُصُولَ with no hamza sign.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ يَا وَلَدِي مَا أَدْرِي أَشْكُرُكَ أَمْ أَشْكُرُ وَالِدَكَ لِأَنَّ دَعْوَتِي الْيَوْمَ كُلَّهَا مِنْ بَعْضِ فَضْلِكَ وَإِحْسَانِكَ وَلَيْسَ عِنْدِي مَنْ يَسْتَحِقُّ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla wa-Allāhi yā waladī mā adrī a-ashkuruka am ashkuru wālidaka li-anna daʿwatī al-yawma kullahā min baʿḍi faḍlika wa-iḥsānika wa-laysa ʿindī man yastaḥiqqu dhālika
sentences.l: And he said: By-God, O my son, I do not know whether I should-thank you or should-thank your father, because my invitation today, all of it, is from some of your favour and your beneficence; and I have not with-me anyone-who deserves that.
sentences.i: He said: "By God, my son, I do not know whether to thank you or your father, for this feast of mine today is entirely a part of your bounty and kindness; and there is no one in my company who deserves such a thing."
sentences.n: The question is asked without a particle of choice beyond أَمْ ('or'): أَشْكُرُكَ أَمْ أَشْكُرُ, 'do I thank you, or do I thank'. The speaker is the host, addressing the young narrator.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّمَا عِنْدِي سَادَةٌ مُحْتَرَمُونَ مِثْلُ زَنْتُوتٍ الْحَمَّامِيِّ وَصُلَيْعٍ الْفَامِيِّ وَسِيلَتٍ الْفَوَّالِ عَكْرَنَةَ الْبَقَّالِ وَحَمِيدٍ الزَّبَّالِ وَسَعِيدٍ الْجَمَّٰلِ وَسُوَيْلِمٍ الْعَتَّالِ وَأَبُو مَكَارِشٍ الْبَلَّانِ وَقَسِيمٍ الْحَارِسِ وَكَرِيمٍ السَّائِسِ
sentences.tr: wa-innamā ʿindī sādatun muḥtaramūna mithlu Zantūtin al-ḥammāmiyyi wa-Ṣulayʿin al-fāmiyyi wa-Sīlatin al-fawwāli ʿAkarnata al-baqqāli wa-Ḥamīdin al-zabbāli wa-Saʿīdin al-jammāli wa-Suwaylimin al-ʿattāli wa-Abū Makārishin al-ballāni wa-Qasīmin al-ḥārisi wa-Karīmin al-sāʾisi
sentences.l: And only-this is with-me: lords, respected-ones, like Zantūt the bath-keeper, and Ṣulayʿ the fūm-seller, and Sīlat the bean-seller, ʿAkarna the grocer, and Ḥamīd the dustman, and Saʿīd the camel-man, and Suwaylim the porter, and Abū Makārish the bath-attendant, and Qasīm the watchman, and Karīm the groom.
sentences.i: "All I have are honoured gentlemen of this sort: Zantūt the bath-keeper, Ṣulayʿ the fūm-seller, Sīlat the bean-seller, ʿAkarna the grocer, Ḥamīd the dustman, Saʿīd the camel-driver, Suwaylim the porter, Abū Makārish the bath-attendant, Qasīm the watchman, and Karīm the groom."
sentences.n: A list of nicknamed tradesmen, each name followed by his trade. Trades: حَمَّامِيّ keeper of a bath-house; فَامِيّ a seller of فُوم (in Lane, wheat or bread-grain, also garlic; the exact wares are uncertain); فَوَّال seller of فُول, broad beans; زَبَّال collector of refuse; جَمَّال camel-driver; عَتَّال porter; بَلَّان bath-attendant; سَائِس groom. The text prints الجمل (no alif), read here as الْجَمَّٰلِ with the dagger alif of the defective spelling; it could instead be الْجَمَلِ 'the camel'. The names do not take the genitive consistently: أَبُو stays in the nominative form after مِثْلُ ... وَ, as in the spoken language, and the names ending in -ة (عَكْرَنَةَ) are treated as diptotes. Sīlat (سيلت) is a printed form I cannot identify.

sentences.t: كُلُّ هَؤُلَاءِ مَا فِيهِمْ ثَقِيلٌ وَلَا مُعَرْبِدٌ وَلَا فُضُولِيٌّ وَلَا مُنَكِّدٌ وَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ رَقْصَةٌ يَرْقُصُهَا وَأَبْيَاتٌ يُنْشِدُهَا
sentences.tr: kullu hāʾulāʾi mā fīhim thaqīlun wa-lā muʿarbidun wa-lā fuḍūliyyun wa-lā munakkidun wa-li-kulli wāḥidin min hāʾulāʾi raqṣatun yarquṣuhā wa-abyātun yunshiduhā
sentences.l: All of these — there is not among them a heavy-one, nor a rowdy-one, nor a meddler, nor a spoil-joy; and for each one of these there is a dance he dances and verses he recites.
sentences.i: Not one of them is tiresome, or rowdy, or nosy, or sour; and each of them has a dance to dance and verses to recite.
sentences.n: ثَقِيل 'heavy' is the Arabic word for a bore, one whose company weighs on the room.

sentences.t: وَأَحْسَنُ مَا فِيهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ مِثْلُ خَادِمِكَ الْمَمْلُوكِ لَا يَعْرِفُونَ كَثْرَةَ الْكَلَامِ وَلَا الْفُضُولَ
sentences.tr: wa-aḥsanu mā fīhim annahum mithlu khādimika al-mamlūki lā yaʿrifūna kathrata al-kalāmi wa-lā al-fuḍūla
sentences.l: And the best of what is in them is that they are like your servant, the owned-one; they do not know much-ness of speech, nor meddling.
sentences.i: And the best thing about them is that they are like your own humble servant: they know nothing of endless chatter or of prying.
sentences.n: خَادِمُكَ الْمَمْلُوكُ, 'your servant the slave', is a self-deprecating formula for 'your humble servant'; here the host applies it to himself.

sentences.t: أَمَّا الْحَمَّامِيُّ فَإِنَّهُ يُغَنِّي عَلَى الدَّرْبَلَةِ شَيْأً مِثْلَ السَّمْرُو يَقُومُ يَرْقُصُ وَيَقُولُ أَنَارَائِحٌ أُمِّي امْلِى جَرَّتِي
sentences.tr: ammā al-ḥammāmiyyu fa-innahu yughannī ʿalā al-darbalati shayʾan mithla al-samrū yaqūmu yarquṣu wa-yaqūlu anārāʾiḥun ummī imlī jarratī
sentences.l: As for the bath-keeper, he sings upon the darbala something like the samrū; he rises, dances, and says: I-am-going, my mother — fill my jar.
sentences.i: As for the bath-keeper, he sings to the beat of the drum something like the samrū, then gets up and dances and cries: "I'm off, Mother — fill my jug!"
sentences.n: الدَّرْبَلَة is presumably a hand-drum (compare Egyptian دَرَبُكَّة, darabukka); I have not found the word in Lane or Hava, so the vowels are a guess. السَّمْرُو is also obscure, probably the name of a tune or dance. أَنَارَائِحٌ is two words written as one (أَنَا رَائِحٌ). امْلِى has the feminine-imperative ending of املئي ('fill'), spelled with final ى and without the hamza, as in the spoken language.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْفَامِيُّ فَإِنَّهُ يَجِئُ بِالْمَعْرِفَةِ أَحْسَنَ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ وَيَرْقُصُ وَيَقُولُ يَا نَائِحَةُ يَاسِتِّي مَاقَصَّرْتِ فَمَا يُخَلِّي لِأَحَدٍ فُؤَادًا مِنَ الضَّحِكِ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-fāmiyyu fa-innahu yajīʾu bi-al-maʿrifati aḥsana min ghayrihi wa-yarquṣu wa-yaqūlu yā nāʾiḥatu yāsittī māqaṣṣarti fa-mā yukhallī li-aḥadin fuʾādan min al-ḍaḥiki ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And as for the fūm-seller, he comes with the know-how better than other-than-him, and dances, and says: O wailing-woman, O my lady, you have not fallen-short! — and he leaves for no one a heart, from the laughing at him.
sentences.i: And as for the fūm-seller, he carries off his turn better than anyone else, and dances and cries: "O mourner, my lady, you have not fallen short!" — and he leaves no one with a heart left, for laughing at him.
sentences.n: بِالْمَعْرِفَةِ is obscure: 'with know-how, with finesse', perhaps 'with his routine'. يَجِئُ is written with the hamza on the yā' as printed. يَاسِتِّي and مَاقَصَّرْتِ are each two words run together; the kasra on the final tā' of ماقصرتِ is the edition's own. أَحْسَنَ is an accusative adverb ('better'), and فُؤَادًا is the 'heart' that the audience loses.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الزَّبَّالُ فَإِنَّهُ يُغَنِّي فَيُوقِفُ الْأَطْيَارَ وَيَرْقُصُ وَيَقُولُ الْخَبَرُ عِنْدَ زَوْجَتِي صَارَ فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَلَهُ مِقْدَارٌ وَهُوَ كِيسٌ خَلِيعٌ وَفِي حُسْنِهِ أَقُ—ولُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-zabbālu fa-innahu yughannī fa-yūqifu al-aṭyāra wa-yarquṣu wa-yaqūlu al-khabaru ʿinda zawjatī ṣāra fī ṣundūqin wa-lahu miqdārun wa-huwa kīsun khalīʿun wa-fī ḥusnihi aqūlu
sentences.l: And as for the dustman, he sings, and so makes-stop the birds, and dances, and says: The news with my wife has-become in a chest, and it has a measure, and it is a dissolute purse — and in his beauty I say:
sentences.i: And as for the dustman, he sings until the very birds stand still, and dances and chants: "The affair at my wife's has ended up in a chest — and a goodly size it is — and a wanton little purse it is." And in praise of his beauty I say:
sentences.n: The dustman's song is obscure and perhaps a riddle with an indecent turn: صُنْدُوق 'chest' and كِيس 'purse' can both be bawdy, and خَلِيع is 'dissolute, shameless', so I give the plain words and do not pretend to a certain sense. The print has a dash inside the last word (اق—ول), a printer's break that I have kept; the word is أَقُولُ, 'I say', and it introduces the verses that follow.

sentences.t:
رُوحِي الْفِدَاءُ لِزَبَّالٍ شُغِفْتُ بِهِ * حُلْوُ الشَّمَائِلِ يَحْكِي الْغُصْنَ مَيَّادَا
جَادَ الزَّمَانُ بِهِ لَيْلًا فَقُلْتُ لَهُ * وَالشَّوْقُ يَنْقُصُ مِنِّي كُلَّمَا زَادَا
أَضْرَمْتَ نَارًا فِي قَلْبِي فَجَاوَبَنِي * لَا غَرْوَ وَإِنْ أَصْبَحَ الزَّبَّالُ وَقَّادَا
sentences.tr:
rūḥī al-fidāʾu li-zabbālin shughiftu bihi * ḥulwu al-shamāʾili yaḥkī al-ghuṣna mayyādā
jāda al-zamānu bihi laylan fa-qultu lahu * wa-al-shawqu yanquṣu minnī kullamā zādā
aḍramta nāran fī qalbī fa-jāwabanī * lā gharwa wa-in aṣbaḥa al-zabbālu waqqādā
sentences.l:
My soul is the ransom for a dustman, I am smitten with him * sweet of the ways-of-being, he resembles the bough, swaying
Time was-generous with him by night, so I said to him * while longing wears-me-down whenever it increases:
You have kindled a fire in my heart, and he answered me * no wonder, even if the dustman has become a stoker
sentences.i: My soul be ransom for a dustman I am mad for, sweet in his ways, a swaying bough. Time brought him to me one night, and I said to him, while longing wore me thinner the more it grew: "You have lit a fire in my heart!" And he answered: "No wonder — the dustman has become a stoker."
sentences.n: The print has marks on all these verse words and they are copied as printed. The joke is on the trade: a zabbāl collects refuse, which fed the furnaces of the baths, so a dustman who kindles fire is no surprise. The rhyme is -ādā throughout, with the rhyme-alif spelled out in مَيَّادَا, زَادَا and وَقَّادَا. It is not certain who the speaker of the middle line is; I take the poet to be addressing the dustman and the dustman to answer in the last.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ كَمُلَ فِي كُلِّوَاحِدٍ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ مَا يُلْهِى الْعُقُولَ مِنَ اللَّهْوِ وَالْمَضْحَكَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad kamula fī kulliwāḥidin min hāʾulāʾi mā yulhī al-ʿuqūla min al-lahwi wa-al-maḍḥakati
sentences.l: And there has-been-completed in each-one of these what diverts the minds, of sport and of laughing-matter.
sentences.i: And each of them is perfect in whatever beguiles the mind, in play and in comedy.
sentences.n: كُلِّوَاحِدٍ is كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ written as one word; the final ى of يُلْهِى is the edition's spelling for يُلْهِي.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ وَلَيْسَ الْخَبَرُ كَالْعِيَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla wa-laysa al-khabaru ka-al-ʿiyāni
sentences.l: Then he said: And the report is not like the seeing-with-eyes.
sentences.i: Then he said: "But hearing is no match for seeing."
sentences.n: A proverb: لَيْسَ الْخَبَرُ كَالْعِيَانِ, 'the report is not like the eyewitnessing'; كَـ here means 'like'.

sentences.t: فَإِنِ اخْتَرْتَ أَنْ تَحْضُرَ عِنْدَنَا فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَيْنَا وَاتْرُكْ رَوَاحَكَ إِلَى أَصْدِقَائِكَ الَّذِينَ عَوَّلْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ini ikhtarta an taḥḍura ʿindanā fa-inna dhālika aḥabbu ilayka wa-ilaynā wa-utruk rawāḥaka ilā aṣdiqāʾika alladhīna ʿawwalta ʿalayhim
sentences.l: So if you choose to be-present with us — for that is dearer to you and to us — then leave your going-off to your friends, those on-whom you have relied.
sentences.i: If you choose to come and join us, that will be better for you and for us; so give up going to those friends of yours on whom you were counting.
sentences.n: The shadda on عَوَّلْتَ is the edition's own. The sentence runs on in the manner of speech: the conditional has no clean apodosis and the imperative وَاتْرُكْ finishes it.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ أَثَرَ الْمَرَضِ وَرُبَّمَا تَمْضِي إِلَى أَقْوَامٍ كَثِيرِينَ الْكَلَامِ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ فِيمَا لَا يَعْنِيهِمْ أَوْ يَكُونُ فِيهِمْ وَاحِدٌ فُضُولِيٌّ يُصَدِّعُ رَأْسَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-inna ʿalayka athara al-maraḍi wa-rubbamā tamḍī ilā aqwāmin kathīrīna al-kalāmi yatakallamūna fīmā lā yaʿnīhim aw yakūnu fīhim wāḥidun fuḍūliyyun yuṣaddiʿu raʾsaka
sentences.l: For upon you is the trace of the illness, and perhaps you will go to people many-ones the speech, they speak about what does-not concern them, or there will be among them one meddler who splits your head.
sentences.i: For you still bear the marks of illness, and you might end up among people who talk without end, chattering about what is no business of theirs, or there may be some busybody among them to split your head with his noise.
sentences.n: كَثِيرِينَ الْكَلَامِ keeps the plural -ūn/-īn ending before a following noun, where Classical grammar would drop the nūn in the construct ('rich-in-speech'); I leave it as printed. The sentence also has no relative particle before يَتَكَلَّمُونَ, a Middle Arabic habit with indefinite nouns.

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ صَغَّرْتَ رُوحَكَ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ
sentences.tr: wa-anta ṣaghgharta rūḥaka min al-maraḍi
sentences.l: And you, you have made-small your self from the illness.
sentences.i: And you have worn yourself small with the sickness.
sentences.n: رُوحَكَ here is 'your self', as in spoken Arabic, rather than 'your spirit'. The sense of صَغَّرْتَ is a little uncertain: 'you have diminished yourself, shrunk' is the likeliest, and the alternative would be صَغُرَتْ رُوحُكَ, 'your spirit has shrunk'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ فِي غَيْرِ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yakūnu dhālika fī ghayri hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: So I said to him: That will-be in other-than this day.
sentences.i: So I said to him, "Let that be on some other day than this."

sentences.t: وَضَحِكْتُ مِنْ قَلْبِ الْغَيْظِ وَقُلْتُ لَهُ اقْضِ شُغْلِي وَأَسِيرُ أَنَا فِي أَمَانِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَتَمْضِي أَنْتَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ḍaḥiktu min qalbi al-ghayẓi wa-qultu lahu iqḍi shughlī wa-asīru anā fī amāni Allāhi taʿālā wa-tamḍī anta ilā aṣḥābika
sentences.l: And I laughed from the heart of the rage, and said to him: Accomplish my business, and I-go, I, in the safe-keeping of God the Exalted, and you-go, you, to your companions.
sentences.i: And I laughed out of the very heart of my fury, and said to him, "Finish my errand, and I shall go in God's keeping, while you go to your friends."
sentences.n: وَأَسِيرُ and وَتَمْضِي are plain indicatives where Classical Arabic would use a jussive or subjunctive after an imperative ('and I will go'); this is the spoken, paratactic style. The pronouns أَنَا and أَنْتَ are added for contrast: you go there, I go home.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهُمْ يَنْتَظِرُونَ قُدُومَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahum yantaẓirūna qudūmaka
sentences.l: For indeed they are-awaiting your arrival.
sentences.i: For they are waiting for your arrival.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَامَوْلَايَ مَا طَلَبْتُ إِلَّا أَنْ أُعَاشِرَكَ بِهَؤُلَاءِ الْأَقْوَامِ الْأَكْيَاسِ أَوْلَادِ النَّاسِ الَّذِينَ مَا فِيهِمْ فُضُولِيٌّ وَلَا كَثِيرُ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yāmawlāya mā ṭalabtu illā an uʿāshiraka bi-hāʾulāʾi al-aqwāmi al-akyāsi awlādi al-nāsi alladhīna mā fīhim fuḍūlī wa-lā kathīru al-kalām
sentences.l: So he-said: "O-my-master, I-sought nothing except that I-bring-you-into-company with these folk, the shrewd-ones, sons-of-the-people, those among-whom there-is no meddler and none abundant-of-speech."
sentences.i: He said, "My lord, all I wanted was to make you the companion of these clever folk, sons of good families, among whom there is no busybody and no chatterer."
sentences.n: يَامَوْلَايَ is printed as one word. أَوْلَادِ النَّاسِ, 'sons of the people', is the stock phrase for respectable, well-bred folk. فُضُولِيّ is the meddler, the man who pokes into what is not his concern; the speaker's pose is that he is the opposite, which the rest of the tale will not bear out. The printed edition writes هؤلاء with a precomposed hamza on the wāw, kept here.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي مُذْنَشَأْتُ مَا أَقْدِرُأُعَا شِرُطْ مَنْ يَسْأَلُ عَمَّنْ لَا يَعْنِيهِ وَلَا أُعَاشِرُ إِلَّا مَنْ أَكُونُ مِثْلِي قَلِيلَ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-innī mudh nashaʾtu mā aqdiru uʿā shiruṭ man yasʾalu ʿamman lā yaʿnīhi wa-lā uʿāshiru illā man akūnu mithlī qalīla al-kalām
sentences.l: For I, since-I-grew-up, am-not-able [to] keep-company-with whoever asks about whom it-does-not-concern-him, and I-keep-company-with none except one-I-am like-me, few-of-speech.
sentences.i: For ever since I was a boy I have never been able to keep company with a man who asks about things that are no business of his; I keep company only with one like myself, sparing of words.
sentences.n: The printed words اقدراعا شرط are mis-divided. The sense is أَقْدِرُ أُعَاشِرُ, 'I am able to keep company', and the break falls inside أُعَاشِرُ, leaving a stray ط (possibly a misprint or a stray letter); I vocalise to the printed division. مُذْنَشَأْتُ is مُذْ نَشَأْتُ run together, with a precomposed hamza as printed. Two verbs sit side by side without أَنْ (أَقْدِرُ أُعَاشِرُ), as the text often does. إِلَّا مَنْ أَكُونُ مِثْلِي is awkward: it can only mean 'except someone of whom I may say that I am his like', i.e. 'except my own sort', and I translate that sense.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّكَ لَوْعَاشَرْتَهُمْ وَرَأَيْتَهُمْ مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً تَتْرُكُ جَمِيعَ أَصْحَابِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innaka law-ʿāshartahum wa-raʾaytahum marratan wāḥidatan tatruku jamīʿa aṣḥābika
sentences.l: For indeed-you, if-you-keep-company-with-them and see-them one single time, you-will-leave all your companions.
sentences.i: For if you once kept their company and saw them, you would give up all your other friends.
sentences.n: لَوْ is followed by a perfect in the if-clause, but the main clause has a bare imperfect (تَتْرُكُ) where Classical Arabic wants a perfect with لَ-. A mild Middle Arabic habit. لَوْعَاشَرْتَهُمْ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ تَمَّمَ اللَّهُ بِهِمْ سُرُورَكَ وَلَابُدَّلِي أَنْ أَحْضُرَ عِنْدَهُمْ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu tammama Allāhu bi-him surūraka wa-lā budda lī an aḥḍura ʿindahum yawman mina al-ayyām
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: "May-God complete, through-them, your gladness; and there-is-no-escape for-me that I-attend with-them one day of the days."
sentences.i: I said to him, "May God complete your happiness through them. As for me, I must visit them one of these days."
sentences.n: تَمَّمَ اللَّهُ is a perfect used as a wish ('may God complete'). وَلَابُدَّلِي runs lā budda li-ī together. يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ, 'a day of the days', means simply 'some day'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَرَدْتُ ذَلِكَ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aradtu dhālika fī hādhā al-yawmi
sentences.l: So he-said: "I-wanted that on this day."
sentences.i: He said, "It was for today that I wanted it."
sentences.n: 'That' (ذَلِكَ) is the visit to his friends just mentioned.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ قَدْ عَوَّلْتَ أَنْ تَمْضِيَ مَعِي إِلَى أَصْدِقَائِي فَدَعْنِي أَمْضِيَ بِمَاتَفَضَّلْتَ بِهِ إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-in kunta qad ʿawwalta an tamḍiya maʿī ilā aṣdiqāʾī fa-daʿnī amḍiya bi-mā tafaḍḍalta bihi ilayhim
sentences.l: So if you-have resolved that you-go with-me to my-friends, then leave-me [that] I-go with-what you-have-graciously-bestowed with-it to-them.
sentences.i: If you have made up your mind to come with me to my friends, then let me take to them what you have so kindly given.
sentences.n: بِمَاتَفَضَّلْتَ is printed as one word; تَفَضَّلَ بِـ is 'to bestow graciously (something)', here the food and drink. The sense is that he would carry the gift ahead of him.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ كُنْتَ لَا بُدَّلَكَ الرَّوَاحُ إِلَى أَصْدِقَائِكَ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ فَأَنَا أَمْضِي بِهَذَا الْإِكْرَامِ الَّذِي أَكْرَمْتَنِي بِهِ وَأَدَعُهُ عِنْدَأَ صْحَابٍ يَأْكُلُونَ وَيَشْرَبُونَ وَلَا يَنْتَظِرُونِي
sentences.tr: wa-in kunta lā budda laka al-rawāḥu ilā aṣdiqāʾika fī hādhā al-yawmi fa-anā amḍī bi-hādhā al-ikrāmi alladhī akramtanī bihi wa-adaʿuhu ʿindaa ṣḥābin yaʾkulūna wa-yashrabūna wa-lā yantaẓirūnī
sentences.l: And if there-is-no-escape for-you the going-forth to your-friends on this day, then I go with-this honour that you-honoured-me with-it, and leave-it with companions who-eat and drink and do-not wait-for-me.
sentences.i: And if you must go to your friends today, then I shall take away this kindness you have shown me and leave it with my companions to eat and drink, and they will not wait for me.
sentences.n: اَلرَّوَاحُ is the going out in the afternoon or evening, a stately word for 'setting out'. The printed عندا صحاب is عِنْدَ أَصْحَابٍ with a misplaced word-break; I follow the print, and the ṣād carries a sukūn because it starts a word that is really the middle of one. بِهَذَا الْإِكْرَامِ, 'with this honour', is the food he was given. The clause ولا ينتظروني means 'let them not wait for me' (ينتظروني has the nūn of the verb plus object suffix, no jussive); Middle Arabic keeps the indicative ending where Classical would drop it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَعُودُ إِلَيْكَ وَأَمْضِي مَعَكَ إِلَى أَصْدِقَائِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma aʿūdu ilayka wa-amḍī maʿaka ilā aṣdiqāʾika
sentences.l: Then I-return to-you and go with-you to your-friends.
sentences.i: Then I will come back to you and go with you to your friends.

sentences.t: فَلَيْسَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ أَصْدِقَايَ حِشْمَةٌ تَمْنَعُنِي عَنْ تَرْكِهِمْ وَأَعُودُ إِلَيْكَ عَاجِلًا أَمْضِي مَعَكَ أَيْنَمَا تَوَجَّهْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-laysa baynī wa-bayna aṣdiqāy ḥishmatun tamnaʿunī ʿan tarkihim wa-aʿūdu ilayka ʿājilan amḍī maʿaka aynamā tawajjahta
sentences.l: For there-is-not between-me and between my-friends any reserve that-prevents-me from leaving-them; and I-return to-you speedily, I-go with-you wherever you-head.
sentences.i: For there is no ceremony between me and my friends to keep me from leaving them; I shall come back to you at once and go with you wherever you are bound.
sentences.n: اصدقاي here is the same word as اصدقائي elsewhere, written without the hamza-seat; I read it aṣdiqāy, as printed. حِشْمَة is the reserve or formality that restrains a man among acquaintances. The last two verbs follow one another with no conjunction (أَعُودُ … أَمْضِي), a quick, spoken run.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَاقُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā ḥawla wa-lāquwwata illā bi-Allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi
sentences.l: So I-said: "There-is-no power and-no-strength except through-God, the High, the Mighty."
sentences.n: The standard formula of resignation in the face of something one cannot avoid. وَلَاقُوَّةَ is printed as one word.
sentences.i: There is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty.

sentences.t: اِمْضِ أَنْتَ إِلَى أَصْدِقَائِكَ وَانْشَرِحْ مَعَهُمْ وَدَعْنِي أَمْضِيَ إِلَى أَصْدِقَايَ وَأَكُونَ مَعَهُمْ فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَنْتَظِرُونِي
sentences.tr: imḍi anta ilā aṣdiqāʾika wa-anshariḥ maʿahum wa-daʿnī amḍiya ilā aṣdiqāy wa-akūna maʿahum fī hādhā al-yawmi fa-innahum yantaẓirūnī
