sentences.l: Go, you, to your-friends and be-expansive-of-heart with-them, and leave-me [that] I-go to my-friends and am with-them on this day, for indeed-they are-waiting-for-me.
sentences.i: You go to your friends and enjoy yourself with them, and let me go to mine and be with them today, for they are waiting for me.
sentences.n: اِنْشَرِحْ, from انشرح صدره, is 'to be glad at heart, to open up'; the 'heart' is understood.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمُزَيِّنُ لَا أَدَعُكَ تَمْضِي وَحْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-muzayyinu lā adaʿuka tamḍī waḥdaka
sentences.l: So he-said, the barber: "I-do-not leave-you [that] you-go alone."
sentences.i: The barber said, "I will not let you go alone."

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ الْمَوْضِعَ الَّذِي أَمْضِي أَنَالَيْهِ لَا يَقْدِرُ أَحَدٌأَنْ يَدْخُلَ فِيهِ غَيْرِى
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu inna al-mawḍiʿa alladhī amḍī anālayhi lā yaqdiru aḥadun an yadkhula fīhi ghayrī
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: "Indeed the place which I-go I-to-it, none is-able to-enter in-it except me."
sentences.i: I said to him, "The place I am going to is one that nobody but me can enter."
sentences.n: أَنَالَيْهِ is أَنَا إِلَيْهِ, 'I to it': the relative clause repeats the pronoun instead of dropping it, and the alif of إِلَى has fallen away in the run-together spelling. غَيْرِى ends in the dotless yā' the edition often uses for the final -ī here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَظُنُّكَ الْيَوْمَ فِي مِيعَادِ وَاحِدَةٍ وَإِلَّا كُنْتَ تَأْخُذُنِي مَعَكَ وَأَنَا أَحَقُّ مِنْ جَمِيعِ النَّاسِ وَأُسَاعِلُكَ عَلَى مَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla aẓunnuka al-yawma fī mīʿādi wāḥidatin wa-illā kunta taʾkhudhunī maʿaka wa-anā aḥaqqu min jamīʿi al-nāsi wa-usāʿiluka ʿalā mā turīdu
sentences.l: So he-said: "I-suppose-you today to-be at an-appointment of one [woman], and otherwise you-would-have-taken me with-you, and I am more-deserving than all the people, and I-would-help-you in what you-want."
sentences.i: He said, "I suspect you have a rendezvous with some woman today; otherwise you would take me with you, for I have more right than anyone, and I could help you in whatever you want."
sentences.n: مِيعَادِ وَاحِدَةٍ is 'the appointment of one (woman)': the feminine واحدة stands for a woman, as the barber's next remark about a foreign woman confirms. This is my reading of an elliptical phrase. وَأُسَاعِلُكَ is probably a misprint for وَأُسَاعِدُكَ, 'and I would help you' (ل for د); I keep the printed letter and vocalise it as if it were a verb of the same pattern. وَإِلَّا is 'if not, otherwise'.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ عَلَى اِمْرَأَةٍ أَجْنَبِيَّةٍ فَتَرُوحَ رُوحُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innī akhāfu an tadkhula ʿalā imraʾatin ajnabiyyatin fa-tarūḥa rūḥuka
sentences.l: For indeed-I fear that you-enter upon a-woman a-stranger, and-so your-spirit goes-off.
sentences.i: For I am afraid you will go in to some strange woman and lose your life.
sentences.n: تَرُوحَ رُوحُكَ, 'your soul goes off', is a play on the root; رُوح here is the spirit or life-breath. دَخَلَ عَلَى is the ordinary idiom for 'go in to someone', and with a woman it carries the sense of a private visit. أَجْنَبِيَّة is a woman not of his kin, a stranger to the household.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ مَدِينَةُ بَغْدَادَ لَا يَقْدِرُ أَحَدٌ يَعْمَلُ فِيهَا شَيْأً مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأَ شْيَاءِ لَا سِيَّمَا فِي مِثْلِ هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَهَذَا وَالِي بَغْدَادَ صَارِمٌ عَظِيمٌ
sentences.tr: fa-inna hādhihi madīnatu baghdāda lā yaqdiru aḥadun yaʿmalu fīhā shayʾan min hādhihi al-ashyāʾi lā siyyamā fī mithli hādhā al-yawmi wa-hādhā wālī baghdāda ṣārimun ʿaẓīmun
sentences.l: For this is the-city of-Baghdad: none is-able to-do in-it anything of these things, least-of-all on a-day like this day; and this governor of-Baghdad is stern, mighty.
sentences.i: For this is Baghdad: nobody can get away with any of these things in it, least of all on a day like this, and the governor of Baghdad is a stern and mighty man.
sentences.n: شَيْأً is printed شياً with the fatḥatān on the alif, as kept here; I add the hamza. The printed الا شياء is الأشياء with a stray space (hence الْأَ شْيَاءِ). 'These things' is the barber's coy way of saying illicit meetings. يَقْدِرُ أَحَدٌ يَعْمَلُ again has no أَنْ.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ وَيْلَكَ يَاشَيْخَ السُّوءِ اِنْقَلِعْ لَايْشِ هَذَا الْكَلَامُ الَّذِي تُقَابِلُنِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu waylaka yāshaykha al-sūʾi inqaliʿ lāysh hādhā al-kalāmu alladhī tuqābilunī bihi
sentences.l: So I-said: "Woe-to-you, O elder of-evil! Pull-yourself-up-by-the-roots! For-what [is] this talk that you-meet me with-it?"
sentences.i: I said, "Damn you, you wretched old man! Be off with you! What is this talk you greet me with?"
sentences.n: اِنْقَلِعْ ('be uprooted', hence 'clear off') is one of the few prose words the edition itself points; its vowels are kept as printed. لَايْشِ is the colloquial contraction of لأيِّ شيء, 'why, what for'. يَاشَيْخَ is printed as one word. شَيْخَ السُّوءِ is 'old man of evil', a stock insult.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِى يَا بَارِدُ تَقُولُ لِي مَا أَسْتَحْيِي وَتُخْفِي عَنِّي وَأَنَا عَلِمْتُ هَذَا وَتَحَقَّقْتُهُ وَإِنَّمَا أَطْلُبُ أَسْأَلُكَ الْيَوْمَ بِنَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī yā bāridu taqūlu lī mā astaḥyī wa-tukhfī ʿannī wa-anā ʿalimtu hādhā wa-taḥaqqaqtuhu wa-innamā aṭlubu asʾaluka al-yawma bi-nafsī
sentences.l: So he-said to-me: "O cold-one, you-say to-me 'I-am-not-ashamed', and you-hide from-me — and I have-known this and ascertained-it — and I only seek [that] I-ask-you today by my-self."
sentences.i: He said to me, "You dull fellow! You tell me you feel no shame, and you keep things from me, though I already know all this and have made sure of it. All I ask, today, is a question — I beg you by my own life."
sentences.n: يَا بَارِد, 'O cold one', is a dismissive vocative for a dull or insipid person. مَا أَسْتَحْيِي is hard to be sure of: as printed it is 'I am not ashamed', but it may stand for مَا اسْتَحْيَيْتَ, 'have you no shame?', with the final letter dropped; I vocalise what is printed. أَطْلُبُ أَسْأَلُكَ puts two verbs together without أَنْ. بِنَفْسِي is an oath, 'by my own life'.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَخَشِيتُ أَنْ تَسْمَعَ أَهْلِي وَجِيرَانِي بِمَقَالَةِ الْمُزَيِّنِ
sentences.tr: qāla fa-khashītu an tasmaʿa ahlī wa-jīrānī bi-maqālati al-muzayyini
sentences.l: He-said: So I-feared that there-hear my-family and-my-neighbours of the-utterance of-the-barber.
sentences.i: I was afraid, he said, that my family and my neighbours would hear what the barber was saying.
sentences.n: قَالَ is the narrator's 'he said', stepping back in to remind us that the tale is being told by the young man. The verb تَسْمَعَ is feminine singular with the plural subject أَهْلِي وَجِيرَانِي, as Arabic often does with a plural of non-agreement; سَمِعَ بِـ is 'to hear of, to hear about'.

sentences.t: فَسَكَتُّ سُكُوتًا طَوِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-sakattu sukūtan ṭawīlan
sentences.l: So I-fell-silent a-silence long.
sentences.i: So I fell silent for a long while.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَنَا وَقْتُ الصَّلَوةِ وَجَاءَ وَقْتُ الْخُطْبَةِ وَقَدْ فَرَغَ حَلْقُ رَأْسِي
sentences.tr: wa-adrakanā waqtu al-ṣalawati wa-jāʾa waqtu al-khuṭbati wa-qad faragha ḥalqu raʾsī
sentences.l: And the-time of-the-prayer overtook-us, and the-time of-the-sermon came, and the-shaving of-my-head had finished.
sentences.i: The hour of prayer overtook us, and the time of the sermon came, by which time the shaving of my head was done.
sentences.n: الصَّلَوة is the Friday congregational prayer; الْخُطْبَة is the sermon that comes with it. The spelling with wāw (الصلوة) is the old one.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ امْضِ إِلَى أَصْحَابِكَ بِهَذَا الطَّعَامِ وَالشَّرَابِ وَأَنَا أَنْتَظِرُكَ حَتَّى تَعُودَ وَتَمْضِيَ مَعِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu imḍi ilā aṣḥābika bi-hādhā al-ṭaʿāmi wa-al-sharābi wa-anā antaẓiruka ḥattā taʿūda wa-tamḍiya maʿī
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: "Go to your-companions with-this food and drink, and I wait-for-you until you-return and go with-me."
sentences.i: I said to him, "Take this food and drink to your companions, and I will wait for you until you come back and go with me."
sentences.n: اِمْضِ بِـ here means 'go off with', i.e. 'take along'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَزَلْ لِهَذَا الْمَلْعُونِ أُدَاهِنُهُ وَأَخْدَعُهُ لَعَلَّهُ يَمْضِيَ عَنِّي
sentences.tr: wa-lam azal li-hādhā al-malʿūni udāhinuhu wa-akhdaʿuhu laʿallahu yamḍiya ʿannī
sentences.l: And I-did-not cease, for this accursed-one, flattering-him and deceiving-him, perhaps he-might-go from-me.
sentences.i: And I kept on coaxing and deceiving that accursed man, hoping he might go away and leave me.
sentences.n: لِهَذَا الْمَلْعُونِ is a dative that points back at the object, 'for this cursed one, I flattered him', a doubling of the pronoun that the Classical language does not need. دَاهَنَ is to cajole, to sweet-talk. The narrator calls the barber الملعون, 'the accursed', from here on.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لِي إِنَّكَ تُخَادِعُنِي وَتَمْضِي وَحْدَكَ وَتَرْمِي نَفْسَكَ فِي مُصِيبَةٍ لَاخَلَاصَ لَكَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lī innaka tukhādiʿunī wa-tamḍī waḥdaka wa-tarmī nafsaka fī muṣībatin lā khalāṣa laka minhā
sentences.l: So he-said to-me: "Indeed-you are-beguiling-me and go alone and throw yourself into a-calamity [of which] there-is-no-escape for-you from-it."
sentences.i: He said to me, "You are deceiving me, and you will go off alone and throw yourself into a disaster you cannot get out of."
sentences.n: لَاخَلَاصَ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَاللَّهَ اللَّهَ لَاتَرُحْ حَتَّى أَعُودَ إِلَيْكَ وَأَمْضِيَ مَعَكَ حَتَّى أَعْلَمَ مَا يَتِمُّ مِنْ أَمْرِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-Allāha Allāha lā taruḥ ḥattā aʿūda ilayka wa-amḍiya maʿaka ḥattā aʿlama mā yatimmu min amrika
sentences.l: So God, God! Do-not-go-off until I-return to-you and go with-you until I-know what will-be-completed of your-affair.
sentences.i: By God, by God, do not leave until I come back to you and go with you, and see how your affair turns out.
sentences.n: فَاللَّهَ اللَّهَ is an accusative of urging, 'mind God, mind God!', a strong appeal. لَاتَرُحْ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ نَعَمْ لَا تُبْطِى عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu naʿam lā tubṭī ʿalayya
sentences.l: So I-said to-him: "Yes; do-not delay on me."
sentences.i: I said to him, "Yes; only do not be long about it."
sentences.n: تُبْطِى is the verb أَبْطَأَ 'to be slow', with the hamza lost and the final written with the dotless yā'. عَلَيَّ here is 'on me', i.e. to my cost.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ جَمِيعَ مَا أَعْطَيْتُهُ لَهُ مِنَ الطَّعَامِ وَالشَّرَابِ وَغَيْرِهِ وَخَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha jamīʿa mā aʿṭaytuhu lahu mina al-ṭaʿāmi wa-al-sharābi wa-ghayrihi wa-kharaja min ʿindī
sentences.l: So he-took all that I-had-given to-him of the-food and the-drink and other-than-it, and went-out from with-me.
sentences.i: He took everything I had given him, food and drink and the rest, and went out from my house.

sentences.t: وَسَلَّمَهُ هَذَا الْمَلْعُونُ إِلَى حَمَّالٍ وَدَّاهُ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَأَخْفَى نَفْسَهُ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَزِقَّاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-sallamahu hādhā al-malʿūnu ilā ḥammālin waddāhu ilā manzilihi wa-akhfā nafsahu fī baʿḍi al-azziqāti
sentences.l: And this accursed-one handed-it to a-porter, who-conveyed-it to his-house, and hid himself in some of-the-lanes.
sentences.i: And that accursed man handed it over to a porter, who took it to his house, and hid himself in one of the alleys.
sentences.n: وَدَّاهُ is the colloquial verb for 'to convey, to take (something) to a place'; it is a Middle Arabic form and no Classical dictionary root is meant. الْأَزِقَّات is a double plural of زُقَاق, 'lane', common in speech. أَخْفَى نَفْسَهُ is 'hid himself'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُمْتُ مِنْ سَاعَتِي وَقَدْ سَلَّمَ الْمُؤَذِّنُونَ
sentences.tr: thumma qumtu min sāʿatī wa-qad sallama al-muʾadhdhinūna
sentences.l: Then I-rose from my-hour, and the-muezzins had given-the-salutation.
sentences.i: Then I got up at that very moment, for the muezzins had already given the closing salutation.
sentences.n: min sāʿatī, 'from my hour', is 'immediately, at once'. سَلَّمَ الْمُؤَذِّنُونَ: the muezzins give their salutation (the blessing on the Prophet) after the call; I read it as the call being finished, which I cannot confirm from the text. The precomposed ؤ in المؤذنون is the edition's own.

sentences.t: فَلَبِسْتُ ثِيَابِي وَخَرَجْتُ وَحْدِي وَأَتَيْتُ إِلَى الزُّقَاقِ وَوَقَفْتُ عَلَى الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي رَأَيْتُ فِيهِ الصَّبِيَّةَ فَوَجَدْتُ الْعَجُوزَ وَاقِفَةً تَنْتَظِرُنِي
sentences.tr: fa-labistu thiyābī wa-kharajtu waḥdī wa-ataytu ilā al-zuqāqi wa-waqaftu ʿalā al-bayti alladhī raʾaytu fīhi al-ṣabiyyata fa-wajadtu al-ʿajūza wāqifatan tantaẓirunī
sentences.l: So I-put-on my clothes and went-out alone, and came to the alley, and stood at the house in-which I-had-seen the girl, and found the old-woman standing, waiting-for-me.
sentences.i: So I put on my clothes and went out alone, and came to the alley and stood before the house where I had seen the girl; and there I found the old woman standing, waiting for me.

sentences.t: فَطَلَعْتُ مَعَهَا إِلَى الطَّبَقَةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الْجَارِيَةُ فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُهَا وَإِذَا بِصَاحِبِ الدَّارِ عَادَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ مِنَ الصَّلَوةِ وَدَخَلَ الْقَاعَةَ وَأَغْلَقَ الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭalaʿtu maʿahā ilā al-ṭabaqati allatī fīhā al-jāriyatu fa-lammā dakhaltuhā wa-idhā bi-ṣāḥibi al-dāri ʿāda ilā manzilihi mina al-ṣalāti wa-dakhala al-qāʿata wa-aghlaqa al-bāb
sentences.l: So I-went-up with her to the storey in-which (was) the girl; and when I-entered-it — and-behold, with-the-master of-the-house: he-had-returned to his dwelling from the prayer, and entered the hall, and bolted the door.
sentences.i: So I went up with her to the floor where the girl was; and no sooner had I gone in than — behold, the master of the house! He had come home from the prayer, gone into the hall, and bolted the door.
sentences.n: The sentence is an anacoluthon: فَلَمَّا دَخَلْتُهَا ('when I entered it') is followed by وَإِذَا, 'and behold', and the main clause is never stated; the surprise itself stands in its place. The بِـ in بِصَاحِبِ is the one that regularly follows إِذَا of sudden appearance and is not translated. الصَّلَوةِ is the edition's spelling, with the waw of the older orthography, and is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَشْرَفْتُ أَنَا مِنَ الطَّاقِ فَرَأَيْتُ هَذَا الْمُزَيِّنَ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ قَاعِدًا عَلَى الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-ashraftu anā mina al-ṭāqi fa-raʾaytu hādhā al-muzayyina laʿnatu Allāhi ʿalayhi qāʿidan ʿalā al-bāb
sentences.l: So I-looked-out, I, from the arch, and saw this barber — the-curse of-God upon-him — sitting at the door.
sentences.i: So I peered out from the arched window and saw that barber — God's curse upon him — sitting at the door.
sentences.n: الطَّاق is an arch or arched opening, here the window-niche over the entrance. The pronoun أَنَا is not needed grammatically after أَشْرَفْتُ; it emphasises the speaker. لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ is a stock curse that the narrator attaches to the barber's name.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ مِنْ أَيْنَ عَلِمَ هَذَا الشَّيْطَانُ بِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu min ayna ʿalima hādhā al-shayṭānu bī
sentences.l: So I-said: From where knew this devil of-me?
sentences.i: I said: How did this devil come to know about me?

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ لِأَمْرٍ يُرِيدُهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ هَتْكِ سِتْرِي أَنَّ جَارِيَةَ صَاحِبِ الدَّارِ إِذْ نَبَتْ عِنْدَهُ فَضَرَبَهَا فَصَاحَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa fī hādhihi al-sāʿati li-amrin yurīduhu Allāhu min hatki sitrī anna jāriyata ṣāḥibi al-dāri idh nabat ʿindahu fa-ḍarabahā fa-ṣāḥat
sentences.l: So it-so-fell-out, in this hour, for a matter God wills — of the-tearing-open of-my veil — that the girl of-the-master of-the-house, when she-recoiled with-him, (then) he-struck her and she-cried-out.
sentences.i: And so it happened, at that very hour, because of something God willed — the tearing away of my cover — that the master's slave-girl displeased him, and he struck her, and she cried out.
sentences.n: هَتْكُ السِّتْر, 'the rending of the veil', is the idiom for public exposure and disgrace. نَبَتْ is read as the feminine perfect of نَبَا, 'to recoil, to prove unsuitable, to fall short'; the edition's spelling could also be a slip for another verb, so the sense 'she displeased him' is the best fit rather than a certainty. The فَ of فَضَرَبَهَا resumes the sentence after the long إِذْ clause, 'when she ... (then) he struck her'; it is not 'and'.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَبْدُهُ لِيُخَلِّصَهَا فَضَرَبَهُ فَصَاحَ الْآخَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿabduhu li-yukhalliṣahā fa-ḍarabahu fa-ṣāḥa al-ākharu
sentences.l: Then his slave entered to-free her, and he-struck him, and the-other cried-out.
sentences.i: Then his manservant came in to free her; he struck him as well, and the other cried out in turn.

sentences.t: فَاعْتَقَلَ الْمُزَيِّنُ الْمَلْعُونُ أَنَّهُ يَضْرِبُنِي فَصَاحَ وَخَرَقَ أَثْوَابَهُ وَحَثَا التُّرَابَ عَلَى رَأسِهِ وَبَقِيَ يَصْرُخُ وَيَسْتَغِيثُ وَالنَّاسُ حَوْلَهُ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ قُتِلَ سَيِّدِي فِي بَيْتِ الْقَاضِي
sentences.tr: fa-iʿtaqala al-muzayyinu al-malʿūnu annahu yaḍribunī fa-ṣāḥa wa-kharaqa athwābahu wa-ḥathā al-turāba ʿalā raʾsihi wa-baqiya yaṣrukhu wa-yastaghīthu wa-al-nāsu ḥawlahu wa-huwa yaqūlu qutila sayyidī fī bayti al-qāḍī
sentences.l: So the-barber, the-cursed, held (that) he is-beating me; and he-cried-out, and tore his garments, and threw the-dust upon his head, and kept crying-out and calling-for-help, with-the-people around him, he saying: My-master has-been-killed in the-house of-the-judge.
sentences.i: The accursed barber got it into his head that the man was beating me, and he screamed, and tore his clothes, and flung dust on his head, and went on shrieking and calling for help, with the crowd all about him, crying: My master has been killed in the judge's house!
sentences.n: اعْتَقَلَ as printed means 'to seize, to hold fast', which does not fit here. The sense wanted is اعْتَقَدَ, 'to hold an opinion, to come to believe', so this is probably a misprint of د as ل; it is pointed as printed and translated by the sense. The gestures of mourning, tearing the clothes and throwing dust on the head, recur through the tale. The barber's cry is a deliberate false alarm: he takes the fall of blows in the judge's house to mean that his master is being murdered.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ مَضَى إِلَى دَارِي وَهُوَ يَصِيحُ وَالنَّاسُ خَلْفَهُ وَأَعْلَمَ أَهْلَ بَيْتِي وَغِلْمَانِي
sentences.tr: thumma maḍā ilā dārī wa-huwa yaṣīḥu wa-al-nāsu khalfahu wa-aʿlama ahla baytī wa-ghilmānī
sentences.l: Then he-went to my house, he crying-out, with-the-people behind him, and informed the-people of-my-house and my lads.
sentences.i: Then he set off for my house, still shouting, with the crowd at his heels, and told my household and my servants.

sentences.t: فَمَا دَرَيْتُ إِلَّا وَهُمْ أَقْبَلُوا مُخَرِّقِينَ الثِّيَابَ وَحَالِّينَ شُعُورَهُمْ يَصِيحُونَ وَاسَيِّدَاهْ وَهَذَا الْمُزَيِّنُ قَدْ أَمَّهُمْ مُخَرِّقَ الثِّيَابِ وَهُوَ يَصِيحُ وَالنَّاسُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā daraytu illā wa-hum aqbalū mukharriqīna al-thiyāba wa-ḥāllīna shuʿūrahum yaṣīḥūna wā-sayyidāh wa-hādhā al-muzayyinu qad ammahum mukharriqa al-thiyābi wa-huwa yaṣīḥu wa-al-nāsu maʿahu
sentences.l: And I knew-not except (that) they had-come on, tearing the-garments and loosing their-hair, crying-out: O-my-master! — and this barber had led-them, tearing-of the-garments, he crying-out, with-the-people with-him.
sentences.i: I knew nothing until they were upon me, tearing their clothes and letting their hair hang loose, shrieking, Alas, our master! — and there was the barber leading them, his own clothes in rags, shouting, with the crowd along with him.
sentences.n: فَمَا دَرَيْتُ إِلَّا وَ... is the idiom of sudden event, 'I knew nothing until ...'. مُخَرِّقِينَ and حَالِّينَ are circumstantial accusatives (how they came); the same word comes again in the singular, مُخَرِّقَ الثِّيَابِ, with its object in the genitive. وَا سَيِّدَاهْ is the wailing call of lament (nudba), 'O my master!'.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا أَهْلِى يَصْرُخُونَ وَهُوَ فِي أَوَائِلِهِمْ يَصْرُخُ وَهُمْ يَقُولُونَ وَاقَتِيلَاهْ وَاقَتِيلَاهْ وَهَمُّوا نَحْوَ الدَّارِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهَا
sentences.tr: qāla wa-lam yazālū ahlī yaṣrukhūna wa-huwa fī awāʾilihim yaṣrukhu wa-hum yaqūlūna wā-qatīlāh wā-qatīlāh wa-hammū naḥwa al-dāri alladhī anā fīhā
sentences.l: He-said: And they-did-not cease, my-people, crying-out, he (being) in their foremost-ones crying-out, and they saying: O-the-slain! O-the-slain! and they-set-out toward the-house which I (am) in-it.
sentences.i: He said: My household never stopped screaming, with him in the forefront of them, screaming too, and they kept crying, Oh, he is slain! Oh, he is slain! and they bore down on the house I was in.
sentences.n: أَهْلِي is printed اهلى, with final ى for ي (a stray spelling kept as printed). The plural verb يَزَالُوا stands before its subject أَهْلِي, a Middle Arabic agreement of the kind a Classical grammar would not give. الدَّارِ is masculine here (الَّذِي) but is picked up by the feminine فِيهَا, as dār usually is; both are left as printed.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ صَاحِبُ الدَّارِ الضَّجَّةَ وَالصُّرَاخَ عَلَى بَابِهِ فَقَالَ لِبَعْضِ غِلْمَانِهِ انْظُرْ مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa ṣāḥibu al-dāri al-ḍajjata wa-al-ṣurākha ʿalā bābihi fa-qāla li-baʿḍi ghilmānihi unẓur mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: So the-master of-the-house heard the-uproar and the-screaming at his door, and said to-some of-his lads: Look — what (is) the-news?
sentences.i: The master of the house heard the uproar and the screaming at his door, and said to one of his servants: Go and see what is the matter.
sentences.n: This is the judge's house, and the man who speaks is its master, the owner of the girl; the lame narrator is still hidden inside it.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ الْغُلَامُ وَعَادَ إِلَى سَيِّدِهِ وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِى عَلَى الْبَابِ أَزْيَدُ مِنْ عَشَرَةِ آلَافِ نَفْسٍ مَا بَيْنَ رَجُلٍ وَامْرَأَةُ وَهُمْ يَصِيحُونَ وَاقَتِيلَاهْ وَيُشِيرُونَ إِلَى دَارِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-ghulāmu wa-ʿāda ilā sayyidihi wa-qāla yā sayyidī ʿalā al-bābi azyadu min ʿashrati ālāfi nafsin mā bayna rajulin wa-imraʾatu wa-hum yaṣīḥūna wā-qatīlāh wa-yushīrūna ilā dārinā
sentences.l: So the-lad went-out and returned to his master and said: O my-master, at the-door (are) more than ten thousands-of persons, of-what (is) between man and woman, and they cry-out O-the-slain! and point to our house.
sentences.i: The servant went out, then came back to his master and said: My lord, at the door there are more than ten thousand souls, men and women together, crying Oh, he is slain! and pointing at our house.
sentences.n: The edition prints a damma on the last letter of وَامْرَأَةُ; it is kept, though the nominative is not what مَا بَيْنَ would govern (a genitive رَجُلٍ وَامْرَأَةٍ would be expected). 'Ten thousand' is the servant's panic, not a count. مَا بَيْنَ رَجُلٍ وَامْرَأَةُ is 'whatever lies between man and woman', i.e. both men and women.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْقَاضِي ذَلِكَ عَظُمَ عَلَيْهِ الْأَمْرُ فَغَضِبَ وَقَامَ وَخَرَجَ وَفَتَحَ الْبَابَ فَرَأَى جَمْعًا عَظِيمًا فَبُهِتَ وَقَالَ يَا قَوْمُ مَا الْقِصَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-qāḍī dhālika ʿaẓuma ʿalayhi al-amru fa-ghaḍiba wa-qāma wa-kharaja wa-fataḥa al-bāba fa-raʾā jamʿan ʿaẓīman fa-buhita wa-qāla yā qawmu mā al-qiṣṣatu
sentences.l: And when the-judge heard that, the-matter grew-great upon him, and he-grew-angry, and rose, and went-out, and opened the-door, and saw a-throng, great; and was-struck-dumb, and said: O people, what (is) the-story?
sentences.i: When the judge heard this, the matter weighed heavily on him; he flew into a rage, got up, went out, and opened the door, and saw an enormous crowd. He stood dumbfounded and said: People, what is the meaning of this?
sentences.n: فَبُهِتَ is the passive of بَهَتَ, 'to be struck dumb, to be astounded'. مَا الْقِصَّةُ, literally 'what is the story?', is the ordinary way of asking what is going on.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ الْغِلْمَانُ يَا مَلْعُونُ يَا كَلْبُ يَا خِنْزِيرُ إِنَّكَ قَتَلْتَ سَيِّدَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu al-ghilmānu yā malʿūnu yā kalbu yā khinzīru innaka qataltā sayyidanā
sentences.l: And they-said to-him, the-lads: O cursed! O dog! O pig! Indeed-you have-killed our-master.
sentences.i: My servants answered him: You accursed man, you dog, you swine! You have killed our master!
sentences.n: الْغِلْمَانُ here are the narrator's own household, who arrived in the earlier sentence, not the judge's; the plural verb with the subject added after it ('they said to him, the lads') is the same loose agreement as above. The plain vocatives are left as insults, as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا قَوْمُ وَمَا الَّذِي فَعَلَهُ سَيِّدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَقْتُلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā qawmu wa-mā alladhī faʿalahu sayyidukum ḥattā aqtulahu
sentences.l: So he-said: O people, and what (is) that-which your-master did, so-that I should-kill him?
sentences.i: He said: People, what did your master ever do that I should kill him?

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿan al-kalāmi al-mubāḥ
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazad, and she-fell-silent from the-permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, leaving the tale she was allowed to tell.
sentences.n: The closing formula of the night; the rhyme is ṣabāḥ / mubāḥ.
